[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 1.9 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"i":0,"status":"fulfilled","value":{"chunk_id":"c373aa","wall_time_seconds":0.6122244,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":2264,"output":"code=0\\r\\nupdated=2026-09-16 01:52:58\\r\\n Accessing the Network Using the Emulator Accessing the Internet Emulators can access the Internet through the network of the local computer. The emulator leverages the local computer\'s Ethernet or WLAN connection, sharing the same network resources. If the network connection fails, check whether local network access is restricted (for example, on a corporate intranet). If network access is restricted, configure a network proxy on the emulator by following the instructions in Network . If a digital certificate is required to access the network, install the digital certificate by following the instructions in How do I install a digital certificate for initiating HTTPS requests . Since the emulator\'s virtual Ethernet remains in a connected state, disconnecting the local computer\'s network or the Wi-Fi within the emulator will not put the emulator into a fully disconnected network state. Since version 26.0.0, network disconnection simulation is supported. Accessing the Local Network Create a network server on the local computer. The emulator can access the server on the local computer through 10.0.2.2:< localPort >. 10.0.2.2 is the default gateway of the emulator. Enabling Mutual Access Between Two Emulators If two emulators need to communicate with each other, perform the following steps: Run emulators A and B on the local computer. The device IP address of the emulator is 10.0.2.15. On emulator B, set the server to listen for 10.0.2.15:< serverPort >. On the local computer, set redirection from the local computer (localhost:< localPort >) to emulator B (10.0.2.15:< serverPort >). For example: hdc -t 127.0.0.1:5555 fport tcp:<localPort> tcp:<serverPort> 127.0.0.1:5555 is the HDC service port number of emulator B, which can be queried using the hdc list targets command. On emulator A, set the client to connect to 10.0.2.2:< localPort >. 10.0.2.2 indicates the default gateway of the emulator. Network Disconnection Simulation Since version 26.0.0, the emulator supports network disconnection simulation. After launching the emulator, swipe down to open the control center and enable airplane mode to simulate network disconnection and debug app behaviors under this condition. \\r\\nor license agreements are considered accepted, and the command-line interaction process is skipped. Scenario-based Simulation Since version 26.0.0, scenario-based feature simulation is supported via the command line. Supported operations include screen rotation, volume control, screen on/off, and shake. [h2]Rotation Emulator -instance { Emulator name } -rotation {left/right} Parameters Name Description -instance (Mandatory) Emulator name. -rotation (Mandatory) Rotation command, which rotates the emulator screen left or right. [h2]Volume Control Emulator -instance { Emulator name } -volume {up/down} Parameters Name Description -instance (Mandatory) Emulator name. -volume (Mandatory) Volume adjustment command, which adjusts the emulator volume up or down. [h2]Screen On/Off Emulator -instance { Emulator name } -power Parameters Name Description -instance (Mandatory) Emulator name. -power (Mandatory) Power control command, which simulates screen on/off. [h2]Shake Emulator -instance { Emulator name } -shake Parameters Name Description -instance (Mandatory) Emulator name. -shake (Mandatory) Shake command, which simulates a shake gesture. [h2]Foldable State Control Emulator -instance { Emulator name } -foldedState { Folded state } Parameters Name Description -instance (Mandatory) Emulator name. -foldedState (Mandatory) Command for device folding and unfolding, which controls the folding state of a foldable device. The supported states vary by device type: Bi-folds and Pura X Max: open | half-open | close Widescreen foldables (excluding Pura X Max): open | close 2-in-1 foldables: open | vertical-open | half-open | close Tri-folds: single | double | triple | left-folded-right-half\\r\\nen downloaded or not downloaded to query. -http_proxy (Optional) Proxy for querying images when the network is restricted. Proxy format: { Proxy protocol }://{ User name }:{ Password }@{ Proxy host name }:{ Port number }. The proxy protocol can be HTTP or HTTPS. If the password contains special characters, the characters must be escaped. Returns Return Description SoftWareVersion Detailed image version number, which can be used to specify the -osVersion parameter during image downloading. deviceType Product type of the emulator, which can be used to specify the -deviceType parameter during image downloading. downloaded Whether the image has been downloaded locally. The value is true or false . osVersion Image version number, which can be used to specify the -osVersion parameter during image downloading. releaseType Release type of the image. upgradable Whether a newer version of the image is available compared with the local image. The value is true or false . $ Emulator -imageList -deviceType phone -downloaded false -http_proxy \\"http://user:password@proxy.proxyserver.com:port\\" [ { \\"SoftWareVersion\\": \\"6.0.0.112\\", \\"deviceType\\": \\"phone\\", \\"downloaded\\": \\"false\\", \\"osVersion\\": \\"HarmonyOS 6.0.1(21)\\", \\"releaseType\\": \\"Release\\", \\"upgradable\\": \\"false\\" }, ... ] Downloading an Image Since DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Beta1, downloading emulator images is supported. Currently, this feature is available only in the Chinese mainland. For details about the supported product types, see Supported Devices . The value is case insensitive. -osVersion (Mandatory) Emulator image version. If the -screen parameter is also set, the -screen parameter takes precedence. This parameter is available only for emulators that support custom screens. [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 0.8 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'DOC=ide-emulator-create\r\n Creating an Emulator When Internet access is available, follow the steps below to create an emulator. For offline environments, refer to the instructions in Deploying an Emulator Offline . On macOS, you may find in the activity monitor that the memory occupied by the emulator process exceeds the configured value. However, the Memory metric displayed in the activity monitor does not reflect the actual physical memory consumed by the emulator process. For more details, see Why does macOS activity monitor show high memory usage of the Emulator . Using a Preconfigured Emulator Since version 6.1.0 Beta2, DevEco Studio provides preconfigured emulators that you can use directly without manual creation (if no emulator exists locally). Currently, this feature is available only in the Chinese mainland. In the device selection drop-down list, select a preconfigured emulator and click . Download the image as prompted, or choose Tools > Device Manager > from the menu bar to download the image. Creating an Emulator Choose Tools > Device Manager from the menu bar, and click Edit in the lower right-corner to set the storage path ( Local Emulator Location ) of the emulator instance. On macOS, emulator instances are stored in ~/.Huawei/Emulator/deployed by default. On Windows, emulator instances are stored in C:\\Users\\ xxx \\AppData\\Local\\Huawei\\Emulator\\deployed by default. On the Local Emulator tab, click New Emulator in the lower-right corner to create an emulator. On the emulator configuration page, you can select a default device template. If this is your first time using the device, click on the right of the device to download the emulator image. You can also update or delete the emulator image for different devices on this page. Click Edit to set the path for storing the image files. By default, these files are stored in ~/Library/Huawei/Sdk for macOS and C:\\Users\\ xxx \\AppData\\Local\\Huawei\\Sdk for Windows. If the configuration page is not displayed properly (for example, the device list is empty), close DevEco Studio, go to the ~/Library/Huawei directory (or C:\\Users\\ xxx \\AppData\\Local\\Huawei on Windows), and delete the DevEcoStudio x.x folder (for example, DevEcoStudio6\r\nhttps://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/harmonyos-guides/ide-emulator-customize-screen-configuration Customizing the Virtual Device Screen\r\nDOC=ide-emulator-devicetype\r\n Supported Devices The following table lists the device types supported by the Emulator in different operating systems. Operating System Device Type Product Type Remarks Windows (x86) macOS (ARM) Phone Bar phone The function of emulating phones on Windows (x86) or macOS (ARM) is only available in the Chinese mainland. Since 6.1.0 (23), the Pura X Max device model has been added to the widescreen foldable phone category. Bi-fold phone Widescreen foldable phone Tri-fold phone Tablet Tablet The function of emulating tablets on Windows (x86) or macOS (ARM) is only available in the Chinese mainland. 2-in-1 device 2-in-1 device The function of emulating 2-in-1 devices on Windows (x86) or macOS (ARM) is only available in the Chinese mainland. 2-in-1 foldable The function of emulating 2-in-1 foldables on Windows (x86) or macOS (ARM) is only available in the Chinese mainland. Wearable Wearable - WearableKid - TV TV The function of emulating TVs on Windows (x86) or macOS (ARM) is only available in the Chinese mainland. Car Car Since version 26.0.0, the function of emulating telematics devices on Windows (x86) or macOS (ARM) is only available in the Chinese mainland. When the x86 Emulator is used, the C++ project and third-party library need to compile .so files of the x86_64 version. Add x86_64 to the value of externalNativeOptions/abiFilters in the project-level or module-level build-profile.json5 file. For details about the compilation configuration, see externalNativeOptions . \r\nDOC=ide-emulator-command-line\r\nfor emulators that support custom screens. For details, see Customizing the Virtual Device Screen . -screen (Optional) Custom screen configuration of the emulator, including screen width, height, DPI, and diagonal length. The format is "width(px) height(px) DPI diagonal(inch)", for example, -screen "1316 2832 560 6.9" . For a bi-fold emulator, two sets of screen parameters are required, corresponding to the unfolded and folded screens, for example, -screen "2200 2480 480 7.8" "1080 2480 480 6.4" . This parameter is available only for emulators that support custom screens. For details, see Customizing the Virtual Device Screen . -storage (Optional) Storage space of the emulator. The value ranges from 2 to 1023 (unit: GB). The default value is 6 GB. For 26.0.0 and later versions, the value ranges from 2 to 100 (unit: GB). -memory (Optional) RAM of the emulator. The value ranges from 2 to 32 (unit: GB). The default value is 4 GB. -hotBoot (Optional) Whether to enable the hot start function of the emulator. The value can be true or false . If this parameter is not specified, the default value false is used. When it is set to true , the snapshot saved at the last shutdown is loaded during startup, and the emulator is restored to its previous state after startup. This parameter is supported since version 26.0.0. Example Emulator -create Mate70Pro -deviceType phone -osVersion "HarmonyOS 6.0.1(21)" -instancePath D:\\Emulator -imageRoot D:\\Sdk -screenProfile "Mate 70 Pro" -storage 8 -memory 16 Deleting an Emulator Since DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Beta1, deleting emulator instances is supported. Note that images are not deleted. Emulator -delete { Emulator name } -instancePath { Emulator instance path } -force Parameters Name Description -delete (Mandatory) Emulator name. -instancePath/-path (Optional) Emulator instance path. If this parameter is not specified, the emulator instance path in DevEco Studio is used by default. -force (Optional) Flag to force deletion of the specified emulator instance. An interactive confirmation ( y / n ) is required. Appending this parameter bypasses the confirmation. Example Emulator -delete Mate70Pro -instancePath D:\\Emulator -force Viewing Emulator Instances Since DevEco Studio 6.0.0 Beta3, viewing emulator instances is supported. Emulator -l\r\n'}]

Starting the Emulator Emulator -start { Emulator name } -path { Emulator instance path } -imageRoot { Emulator image path } -hdcport { HDC port number } -bootMode { Boot mode } -noWindow Parameters Name Description -hvd/-start (Mandatory) Emulator name. Since DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Beta1, the -start parameter is added. You are advised to use -start . You need to agree to the HarmonyOS Software License and Service Agreement upon the first use. -path/-instancePath (Mandatory) Emulator instance path. Since DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Beta1, this parameter is optional, and the -instancePath parameter is added. You are advised to use -instancePath . If this parameter is not specified, the emulator instance path in DevEco Studio is used by default. -imageRoot (Mandatory) Emulator image path. Since DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Beta1, this parameter is optional. If this parameter is not specified, the emulator image path in DevEco Studio is used by default. -hdcport (Optional) HDC port number. The value ranges from 10000 to 16555. This parameter is supported since DevEco Studio 6.0.1 Beta1. -bootMode (Optional) Emulator startup mode. This parameter is supported since DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Release. If this parameter is not specified, the emulator follows the startup mode configured upon creation. The emulator uses the hot start ( snapshot ) mode if Quick Boot was enabled during creation, or the -hotBoot true parameter was applied via the command line. Otherwise, it runs in cold start ( coldboot ) mode. coldboot : full power-on startup. User data such as installed apps and uploaded files is retained from the previous session unless manually cleared. snapshot : hot start, which loads the snapshot saved at the last shutdown during startup and restores the emulator to its previous state. To use this parameter, enable Quick Boot when creating the emulator or add the -hotBoot true parameter when creating the emulator using the command line. reset : full power-on startup after data is cleared. -noWindow (Optional) Flag to start the emulator in headless mode. This parameter is mandatory for Linux environments without a GUI and is supported since version 26.0.0. Example # DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Beta1 or later Emulator -start "my Emulator" -instancePath D:\\Emulator -imageRoot D:\\Sdk # Versions earlier than DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Beta1 Emulator -hvd "my Emulator" -path D:\\Emulator -imageRoot D:\\Sdk If you are required to log in to your developer account to use the Emulator in DevEco Studio, the Emulator of this version cannot be started using the CLI. In this case, start the Emulator in DevEco Studio. Stopping the Emulator Emulator -stop { Emulator name } Example Emulator -stop "my Emulator" Configuring an Emulator Since DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Beta1, you can configure the emulator instance path, image path, and network proxy. Emulator -config -instancePath { Emulator instance path } -imageRoot { Emulator image path } -http_proxy { Network proxy } Parameters Name Description -config (Mandatory) Emulator configuration command. -instancePath/-path (Optional) Emulator instance path. The specified path must exist and can contain only letters, digits, spaces, hyphens (-), and underscores (_). If an emulator instance is running, this parameter cannot be modified. -imageRoot (Optional) Emulator image path. The specified path must exist and can contain only letters, digits, spaces, hyphens (-), and underscores (_). If an emulator instance is running, this parameter cannot be modified. -http_proxy (Optional) Network proxy. Proxy format: { Proxy protocol }://{ User name }:{ Password }@{ Proxy host name }:{ Port number }. The proxy protocol can be HTTP or HTTPS. If the password contains special characters, the characters must be escaped. Example Emulator -config -instancePath D:/Emulator -imageRoot D:/Sdk -http_proxy "http://user:password@proxy.proxyserver.com:port" Clearing Emulator Configurations Since DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Beta1, you can clear emulator configurations, including the emulator instance path, image path, and network proxy. Emulator -unset instancePath/path/imageRoot/http_proxy Parameters Name Description -unset (Mandatory) Command for clearing emulator configurations. Only one configuration can be cleared at a time. The following configurations can be cleared: instancePath/path : Restores the emulator instance path in DevEco Studio to the default path. imageRoot : Restores the emulator image path in DevEco Studio to the default path. http_proxy : Clears the network proxy configuration. Example Emulator -unset instancePath Viewing/Updating the Product List Since DevEco Studio 6.1.0 Beta1, you can view the product list of the emulator, including the device models and screen parameters\r\nhvd.ini.encoding=UTF-8\r\npath=D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/traces/baseline-round-01/emulator-instances/VgSpec1Baseline\r\n\r\nName\r\n----\r\nHarmonyOS-6.0.31\r\n\r\n'}]

[华为官方模拟器网络教程：Network Disconnection Simulation](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/harmonyos-guides/ide-emulator-access-network#section115741355151910)给出了实际入口：**从26.0.0开始，启动模拟器，下拉控制中心，开启飞行模式，可模拟网络断开。**该页同时解释旧虚拟Ethernet一直连接，断开宿主网络或模拟器Wi-Fi不能让模拟器达到完全断网。官方正文metadata updatedDate为2026-09-16。\n+3. 官方最新[模拟器CLI教程](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/harmonyos-guides/ide-emulator-command-line)继续示范创建旧 API21 镜像，新增参数 `-hotBoot` 等明确标注26.0.0。新工具并非只允许API26镜像；但本文未找到**API23镜像必定支持新增飞行模式断网**的明文承诺，必须用新独立实例实测，不能用推断改矩阵。\n+4. 或官方独立Emulator包，**只接受实际元数据版本为26.0.0.400或更新且正式文档确认断网能力的包**。不要只凭DevEco目录名或下载文件名认版本。\n+\n+root实际安装前保存：来源官网/索引URL、最终重定向URL、官方元数据中的版本/文件大小/摘要（如有）、本地下载SHA256；校验不一致不得执行。若只有本地自算哈希而无官方期望摘要，应明确标为完整性指纹，不能称已完成“官方哈希比对”。Windows若有Authenticode签名可另记 静默代替尚未成立的许可授权。\n+\n+## 4. 可直接执行的新实例流程（仅root/设备角色执行）\n+\n+### 4.1 创建前\n+\n+1. 加载 `D:/HCUP/.hcup-local/Enter-HarmonyEnv.ps1`；使用新工具绝对路径调用 `-version`、`-help -create`、`-help -start`，保存输出。\n+2. 检查新包 SHA256、设备updateTime，按照既有fixture准备本地哨兵、云端备份和UI0。\n+\n+### 4.3 新版API23断网能力闸门\n+\n+先单独验证网络设施，再计产品用例，顺序为**在线前测→飞行模式ON→离线观测→飞行模式OFF→在线恢复**。\n+\n+- 在线前测：HDC11237可执行 `shell echo`、UI树可获取；记录eth0/地址、路由、NetConn/Ethernet dump和系统控制中心。独立真实网络探针至少一个IP直连成功；可使用host运行的可控HTTP服务经guest `10.0.2.2:<port>` 访问，保存实际到达的请求nonce。官方说明10.0.2.2为guest到host的默认网关。先确认这个服务活着，不用错误端点。\n+- 切换：按官方入口在**新版本题实例**下拉控制中心打开飞行模式。记录操作前后截图/树、准确时间、实际工具版本/guest版本。\n+- 离线判定：系统网络原文应支持“失去可用默认网络/虚拟链路断开”等实际状态变化，同时同一IP探针连接失败、活服务无对应nonce请求；记录DNS无关结果。可以保留eth0的静态地址，不能只因地址仍在就否定断网，也不能只因飞行图标变蓝就认定断网。若NetConn仍有可用默认网络、链路/探针均保持成功，则不满足。若只100%丢包而系统仍宣告可用，只能先报传输隔离，不能冒称已获得系统offline信号。\n+- 探针实现：优先使用设备已有的curl/nc或等价正常socket工具；先在在线时证明它能成功，权限错误/命令缺失/ICMP本来不通不能作为断网。若需诊断程序，只能是本题logs下独立诊断产物，普通网络socket，不改生产HAP、不授root、不加应用断网分支。\n+- 控制判定：飞行模式ON期间 `hdc -t 127.0.0.1:11237 shell echo`、UI树、点击命令仍成功，才能开始Hypium。HDC走host loopback控制端口，预期不受guest虚拟Ethernet影响，但官方未保证所有版本组合，必须实测；若失联，用新实例可见控制中心关闭飞行模式恢复，再研究，不能把失联后的用例算完成。\n+- 恢复判定：关闭飞行模式，等待系统默认网络/链路恢复，同一probe重新到达；HDC仍在线。恢复前后都保存原始证据。\n+\n+若新版工具识别API23但断网仍不成立，说明**新host工具+旧guest组合尚未兑现功能**。不改旧镜像，不扩大到root/私有接口；下一步仅在新目录新建官方26镜像的本题专用实例补测，并保留同一冻结HAP与数据fixture。API23继续作为原13+2测试设备证据，API26只补真实断网，并如实登记设备差异；是否还需在新设备重跑完整集由root按测试清单裁定，不能混称同一环境。\n+\n+## 5. R27补测与真实网络归因\n+\n+1. 保存在线系统状态和独立probe成功证据，确认本题HAP、1308×2880/560dpi、自动同步checked=false、本地D0/UI0与有效配置。\n+2. 打开新版飞行模式，独立验证系统offline及HDC存活；正式产品计数窗口开始前停止诊断probe。\n+3. WebDAV配置使用真实活服务的guest可达地址 `http://10.0.2.2:<port>`，避免用 `hdc rport` 形成即使guest NIC断开仍可通过控制通道访问的localhost旁路。fixture在在线时保存，产品用例期间不修改配置。\n+4. 清零受控WebDAV服务日志（在点击前），保存D0/UI0。点击恢复，第一层应立即出现精确标题/正文/按钮；等待仍第一层，N-restore=0、N-download=0、D0不变。\n+5. 取消按钮、真实系统侧滑返回、外部点击各独立执行，检查取消后五按钮和两个结果区回到UI0；没有晚发请求/导入，立即重开仍正常。若只补一个用例，也要确保已发布的离线场景清单要求未被省略。\n+6. 关闭飞行模式，独立probe及系统网络恢复；再验证本题可继续正常操作。既有延迟/503/拒绝连接证据保留为另三条件，不混成offline。\n+\n+记录至少包含：工具包来源与hash、工具版本、guest版本、屏幕配置、HAP哈希/安装时间、在线/离线/恢复的网络原文、探针nonce/请求、飞行模式UI、HDC心跳、第一层与三取消UI树、WebDAV请求零计数窗、本地数据语义摘要、Hypium结果。正式离线期间业务本来就不应发请求，因此“服务端零请求”本身不能证明离线，必须依赖独立设施探针与系统状态。\n+\n+## 6. 影响范围、恢复及不选策略\n+\n+| 策略 | 影响与恢复 | 判断 |\n+| --- | --- | --- |\n+| 新26工具+本题API23新实例 | 仅新实例虚拟网络与新工具目录；飞行OFF恢复，必要时正常关闭新实例。旧11235/工具/数据盘不变。 | 首选，官方明确支持，API23组合需实测。 |\n+| 新26工具+本题26新实例 | 多一个新镜像/实例磁盘和RAM；原工程构建环境不变。飞行OFF、关闭新实例恢复。 | 仅API23组合不支持时后备，不需要其他实体设备。 |\n+| 宿主按Emulator.exe的Windows防火墙Block | 官方Program条件绑定可执行路径，不是精确PID；同路径后来启动的其他实例也会受影响。可能影响loopback/HDC，当前token不提升。规则删除可恢复但需要管理员。 | root已选择无需走此路；不执行，不称精确本题PID隔离。 |\n+| 暂停/终止Emulator、死代理、端点拒绝连接 | 前者破坏guest运行/控制，后两者仅改变某连接条件。 | 不能替代真实系统offline。 |\n+| 旧6.1飞行模式、关Wi-Fi、断宿主网、smode/私有dump写命令 | 官方已解释旧虚拟Ethernet问题；root拒绝已有。 | 不重复，不绕过，不碰宿主全局网络。 |\n+\n+新版断网入口、官方包实际安装和API23能力闸门尚未执行。文档提供可执行路径，不宣告R27通过；主Agent完成设施闸门与产品补测后再更新矩阵/状态。无生产实现调整需求，现有代码继续冻结。\n*** End Patch"));

保持应用endpoint和fixture不变。执行一轮第一层明确继续作为**设施负控**，观察真实应用同一NAT下载链失败，完整保存阶段/UI/错误与时间；服务端该guest窗口应零HEAD/GET到达。配置校验失败、错误密码、备份解密失败、服务未运行等都不能替代网络隔离，因为G0必须证明相同条件成功。\n+4. 负控会真实启动既有恢复任务；原超时包装不能取消底层Promise，**恢复网络前必须等该任务确实结束，或明确强停本题应用清除悬挂请求**。不得在悬挂任务存在时恢复网络，造成迟到GET/预览或污染请求窗口。强停/重启只针对本题应用，D0需复核；不停止模拟器。\n+\n+G2若未成立：记设施前置未满足，保留失败证据；向用户报告哪条NAT仍可达或缺哪些系统观测，再调整其手动操作方法。不能改产品、改验收口径或把拒绝连接/死代理改名offline。\n+\n+### G3：在已确认的手动离线状态跑R27产品补测\n+\n+G2完成且无悬挂恢复任务后，重新进入设置/WebDAV，复核same On the Rule Type page of the New Outbound Rule wizard, select Custom, and then select Next\\n\\nNote\\n\\nAlthough you can create rules by selecting Program or Port, those choices limit the number of pages presented by the wizard. If you select Custom, you see all of the pages, and have the most flexibility in creating your rules.\\n\\n  5. On the Program page, select All programs, and then select Next\\n  6. On the Protocol and Ports page, select the protocol type that you want to block. To restrict the rule to a specified port number, you must select either TCP or UDP. Because this rule is an outbound rule, you typically configure only the remote port number If you select another protocol, then only packets whose protocol field in the IP header matches this rule are blocked by Windows Defender Firewall. Network traffic for protocols is allowed as long as other rules that match don\'t block it. To select a protocol by its number, select Custom from the list, and then type the number in the Protocol number box. When you\'ve configured the protocols and ports, select Next\\n  7. On the Scope page, you can specify that the rule applies only to network traffic to or from the IP addresses entered on this page. Configure as appropriate for your design, and then select Next\\n  8. On the Action page, select Block the connection, and then select Next\\n  9. On the Profile page, select the network location types to which this rule applies, and then select Next\\n  10. On the Name page, type a name and description for your rule, and then select Finish\\n\\n## Create an inbound program or service rule\\n\\nThis type of rule allows the program to listen and receive inbound network traffic on any port.\\n\\nNote\\n\\nThis type of rule is often combined with a program or service rule. If you combine the rule types, you get a firewall rule that limits traffic to a specified port and allows the traffic only when the specified program is running. The program cannot receive network traffic on other ports, and other programs cannot receive network traffic on the specified port. To combine the program and port rule types into a single rule, follow the steps in the Create an Inbound Port Rule procedure in addition to the steps in this procedure.\\n\\nTo create an inbound firewall rule for a program or service:\\n\\n  1. Open the Windows Firewall with Advanced Security console\\n\\n  2. In the navigation pane, select Inbound Rules\\n\\n  3. Select Action, and then select New rule\\n\\n  4. On the Rule Type page of the New Inbound Rule Wizard, select Custom, and then select Next\\n\\nNote\\n\\nInformation the user should notice even if skimmingAlthough you can create rules by selecting Program or Port, those choices limit the number of pages presented by the wizard. If you select Custom, you see all of the pages, and have the most flexibility in creating your rules.\\n\\n  5. On the Program page, select This program path\\n\\n  6. Type the path to the program in the text box. Use environment variables, where applicable, to ensure that programs installed in different locations on different computers work correctly.\\n\\nIf the result is `NONE`, then a firewall rule cannot be applied to that service.\\n\\nTo set a SID type on a service, run the following command: `sc sidtype <ServiceName> <Type>`\\n\\nIn the preceding command, the value of `<Type>` can be `UNRESTRICTED` or `RESTRICTED`. Although the command also permits the value of `NONE`, that setting means the service cannot be used in a firewall rule as described here. By default, most services in Windows are configured as `UNRESTRICTED`. If you change the SID type to `RESTRICTED`, the service might fail to start. We recommend that you change the SID type only on services that you want to use in firewall rules, and that you change the SID type to `UNRESTRICTED`.\\n\\n  8. It is a best practice to restrict the firewall rule for the program to only the ports it needs to operate. On the Protocols and Ports page, you can specify the port numbers for the allowed traffic. If the program tries to listen on a port different from the one specified here, it is blocked. For more information about protocol and port options, see Create an Inbound Port Rule. After you have configured the protocol and port options, select Next\\n\\n  9. On the Scope page, you can specify that the rule applies only to network traffic to or from the IP addresses entered on this page. Configure as appropriate for your design, and then select Next\\n\\n  10. On the Action page, select Allow the connection, and then select Next\\n\\n  11. On the Profile page, select the network location types to which this rule applies, and then select Next\\n\\n  12. On the Name page, type a name and description for your rule, and then select Finish\\n\\n## Create an outbound program or service rule\\n\\nBy default, Windows Defender Firewall allows all outbound network traffic unless it matches a rule that prohibits the traffic. This type of rule prevents the program from sending any outbound network traffic on any port. To create an outbound firewall rule for a program or service:\\n\\n  1. Open the Windows Firewall with Advanced Security console\\n  2. In the navigation pane, select Outbound Rules\\n  3. Select Action, and then select New rule\\n  4. On the Rule Type page of the New Outbound Rule Wizard, select Custom, and then select Next\\n\\nNote\\n\\nAlthough you can create many rules by selecting Program or Port, those choices limit the number of pages presented by the wizard. If you select Custom, you see all of the pages, and have the most flexibility in creating your rules.\\n\\n  5. On the Program page, select This program path\\n  6. Type the path to the program in the text box. Use environment variables as appropriate to ensure that programs installed in different locations on different computers work correctly\\n  7. Do one of the following:\\n     * If the executable file contains a single program, select Next\\n     * If the executable file is a container for multiple services that must all be blocked from sending outbound network traffic, select Customize, select Apply to services only, select OK, and then select Next\\n     * If the executable file is a container for a single service or contains multiple services but the rule only applies to one of them, select Customize, select Apply to this service, and then select the service from the list. If the service does not appear in the list, then select Apply to service with this service short name, and type the short name for the service in the text box. Select OK, and then select Next\\n  8. If you want the program to be allowed to send on some ports, but blocked from sending on others, then you can restrict the firewall rule to block only the specified ports or protocols. On the Protocols and Ports page, you can specify the port numbers or protocol numbers for the blocked traffic. If the program tries to send to or from a port number different from the one specified here, or by using a protocol number different from the one specified here, then the default outbound firewall behavior allows the traffic. For more information about the protocol and port options, see Create an Outbound Port Rule. When you have configured the protocol and port options, select Next\\n  9. On the Scope page, you can specify that the rule applies only to network traffic to or from the IP addresses entered on this page. Configure as appropriate for your design, and then select Next\\n  10. On the Action page, select Block the connection, and then select Next\\n  11. On the Profile page, select the network location types to which this rule applies, and then select Next\\n  12. Provide feedback\\nShow 2 more\\n\\nWindows Firewall is a security feature that helps to protect your device by filtering network traffic that enters and exits your device. This traffic can be filtered based on several criteria, including source and destination IP address, IP protocol, or source and destination port number. Windows Firewall can be configured to block or allow network traffic based on the services and applications that are installed on your device. This allows you to restrict network traffic to only those applications and services that are explicitly allowed to communicate on the network.\\n\\nThe following table lists the Windows editions that support Windows Firewall:\\n\\nExpand table\\n\\nWindows Pro  | Windows Enterprise  | Windows Pro Education/SE  | Windows Education\\n--- | --- | --- | ---\\nYes  | Yes  | Yes  | Yes\\n\\nWindows Firewall license entitlements are granted by the following licenses:\\n\\nExpand table\\n\\nWindows Pro/Pro Education/SE  | Windows Enterprise E3  | Windows Enterprise E5  | Windows Education A3  | Windows Education A5\\n--- | --- | --- | --- | ---\\nYes  | Yes  | Yes  | Yes  | Yes\\n\\nFor more information about Windows licensing, see Windows licensing overview.\\n\\n## Concepts\\n\\nThe default behavior of Windows Firewall is to:\\n\\n  * block all incoming traffic, unless solicited or matching a rule\\n  * allow all outgoing traffic, unless matching a rule\\n\\n### Firewall rules\\n\\nFirewall rules identify allowed or blocked network traffic, and the conditions for this to happen. One example of the exception filters is the quarantine default inbound loopback exception filter.\\nDuring quarantine, all new inbound connections without exceptions are blocked.\\n\\nThis document describes the quarantine feature and explains why the application traffic could be blocked by quarantine.\\n\\n## Quarantine filters\\n\\nThe quarantine feature creates filters that can be split into three categories:\\n\\n  * Quarantine default inbound block filter\\n  * Quarantine default exception filters\\n  * Interface unquarantine filters\\n\\nThese filters are added in the `FWPM_SUBLAYER_MPSSVC_QUARANTINE` sublayer and these layers are:\\n\\n  1. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V4`\\n  2. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V6`\\n  3. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V4`\\n  4. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V6`\\n\\nNote\\n\\nAny firewall rules added by policy settings don\'t affect the filters in the quarantine sublayer. Filters from firewall rules are added in the `FWPM_SUBLAYER_MPSSVC_WF` sublayer. In other words, you can\'t add your own exception filters to prevent packets from being evaluated by quarantine filters.\\n\\nFor more information about WFP layers and sublayers, see WFP Operation.\\n\\n### Quarantine default inbound block filter\\n\\nThe quarantine default inbound block filter blocks any new nonloopback inbound connections, unless the packet isn\'t explicitly permitted by another filter in the quarantine sublayer.\\n\\n### Quarantine default exception filters\\n\\nWhen the interface is in quarantine state, the quarantine default exception filters permit new inbound connections given that they meet the conditions of an exception filter. One example of the exception filters is the quarantine default inbound loopback exception filter. This exception filter allows all loopback packets when the interface is in quarantine state.\\n\\n### Interface unquarantine filter\\n\\nThe interface unquarantine filters allow all nonloopback packets if the interface is successfully categorized.\\n\\n## Quarantine flow\\n\\nThe following events describe the general flow of quarantine:\\n\\n  1. There\'s some change on the current network interface\\n  2. The interface unquarantine filters don\'t permit new inbound connections. The interface is now in quarantine state\\n  3. All nonloopback inbound connections are either permitted by quarantine default exception filters or dropped by the quarantine default inbound block filter\\n  4. The WFP filters applicable to the old interface state are removed\\n  5. The WFP filters applicable to the new interface state are added, which include the unquarantine filters for this interface. These filters are updated to match the interface\'s current state\\n  6. The interface has now exited quarantine state as the interface unquarantine filters permit any new nonloopback packets\\n\\n## Quarantine diagnostics\\n\\nThere are two methods of identifying packet drops from the quarantine default inbound block filter.\\n\\nGiven that the network connectivity issue is reproducible, diagnostic traces can be collected by running the following in an administrative command prompt:\\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\nNew-NetFirewallRule (NetSecurity) | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/netsecurity/new-netfirewallrule?view=windowsserver2019-ps)\\n\ue200cite\ue202turn21search3\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 6 days ago; This example creates an outbound firewall rule to block all of the traffic from the local computer that originates on TCP port 80. ... More specifically, in scenarios involving Teredo traffic, the IPV6_PROTECTION_LEVEL socket option is specified. It is recommended that host firewall implementations maintain the following filters to selectively allow Teredo traffic for an application, while blocking traffic by default for any application without an exemption.\\n\\n## Default Block Filter for Edge Traversed Traffic\\n\\nA host firewall must always maintain a default block filter within the ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V6 filtering layer for traffic matching the specified Interface Type Tunnel and Tunnel Type Teredo conditions. Case 8: Debugging Past Drop - UWP app connects to Internet target address with all capabilities\\nShow 7 more\\n\\nThis document is intended to help network admins, support engineers, and developers to investigate UWP app network connectivity issues.\\n\\nThis document guides you through steps to debug Universal Windows Platform (UWP) app network connectivity issues by providing practical examples.\\n\\n## Typical causes of connectivity issues\\n\\nUWP app network connectivity issues are typically caused by:\\n\\n  1. The UWP applications not being permitted to receive loopback traffic. This permission must be configured. By default, UWP applications aren\'t allowed to receive loopback traffic\\n  2. The UWP app is missing the proper capability tokens\\n  3. The private range is configured incorrectly. For example, the private range is set incorrectly through GP/MDM policies, etc.\\n\\nTo understand these causes more thoroughly, there are several concepts to review.\\n\\nThe traffic of network packets (what\'s permitted and what\'s not) on Windows is determined by the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP). When a UWP app or the private range is configured incorrectly, it affects how the UWP app\'s network traffic will be processed by WFP.\\n\\nWhen a packet is processed by WFP, the characteristics of that packet must explicitly match all the conditions of a filter to either be permitted or dropped to its target address. Connectivity issues typically happen when the packet doesn\'t match any of the filter conditions, leading the packet to be dropped by a default block filter. The presence of the default block filters ensures network isolation for UWP applications. Specifically, it guarantees a network drop for a packet that doesn\'t have the correct capabilities for the resource it\'s trying to reach. Such a packet drop ensures the application\'s granular access to each resource type and preventing the application from escaping its environment.\\n\\nFor more information on the filter arbitration algorithm and network isolation, see Filter Arbitration and Isolation.\\n\\nThe following sections cover debugging case examples for loopback and non-loopback UWP app network connectivity issues.\\n\\n## Debugging UWP App Loopback scenarios\\n\\nIf you need to establish a TCP/IP connection between two processes on the same host where one of them is a UWP app, you must enable loopback.\\n\\nTo enable loopback for client outbound connections, run the following command at a command prompt:\\n\\nWindows Command Prompt\\n\\nCopy\\n    \\n    `CheckNetIsolation.exe LoopbackExempt -a -n=<AppContainer or Package Family>\\n    `\\n\\nTo enable loopback for server inbound connections, run the following command at a command prompt:\\n\\nWindows Command Prompt\\n\\nCopy\\n    \\n    `CheckNetIsolation.exe LoopbackExempt -is -n=<AppContainer or Package Family>\\n    `\\n\\nYou can ensure loopback is enabled by checking the appx manifests of both the sender and receiver.\\n\\nFor more information about loopback scenarios, see Communicating with localhost (loopback).\\n\\nNote\\n\\nIf you are in the middle of developing a UWA application and want to test its loopback, ensure to uninstall and re-install the UWA app if the network capabilities change for whatever reason.\\n\\nAlso, see How to enable loopback and troubleshoot network isolation (Windows Runtime apps).\\n\\n## Debugging Live Drops\\n\\nIf the issue happened recently, but you find you aren\'t able to reproduce the issue, go to Debugging Past Drops for the appropriate trace commands.\\n\\nIf you can consistently reproduce the issue, then you can run the following command in an admin command prompt to gather a fresh trace:\\n\\nConsole\\n\\nCopy\\n    \\n    `Netsh wfp capture start keywords=19\\n    <Run UWP app>\\n    Netsh wfp capture stop\\n    `\\n\\nThese commands generate a wfpdiag.cab. Network drops from Universal Windows Platform (UWP) default inbound/outbound block filters are often caused by the UWP app not being configured correctly (that is, the UWP app is missing the correct capability tokens or loopback isn\'t enabled) or the private range is configured incorrectly.\\nThe change in ID makes the diagnosis process error-prone and difficult.\\n\\nTo debug packet drop events correctly and efficiently, you need more context about the blocking filter, such as its origin. The blocking filters can be categorized under these filter origins:\\n\\n  1. Firewall rules\\n  2. Firewall default block filters\\n    1. AppContainer loopback\\n    2. Boot time default\\n    3. Quarantine default\\n    4. Query user default\\n    5. Stealth\\n    6. Universal Windows Platform (UWP) default\\n    7. Windows Service Hardening (WSH) default\\n\\nThe next section describes the improvements made to audits `5157` and `5152` in Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022, and how the filter origins are used in these events.\\n\\n## Improved firewall audit\\n\\nStarting in Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022, two new fields added to the audit `5157` and `5152` events are Filter Origin and Interface Index:\\n\\n  * The Filter Origin field helps identify the cause of the drop. Packet drops from firewall are explicitly dropped by default block filters created by the Windows Firewall service or a firewall rule that may be created by users, policies, services, apps, etc. \\n## Firewall default block filters\\n\\n### AppContainer loopback\\n\\nNetwork drop events from the AppContainer loopback block filter origin occur when localhost loopback isn\'t enabled properly for the Universal Windows Platform (UWP) app:\\n\\n  * To enable localhost loopback in a local debugging environment, see Communicating with localhost\\n  * To enable localhost loopback for a published app At key points in the TCP/IP stack there are filtering layers where network data is passed to the filter engine for processing. Filters in the filter engine can specify a callout for the filter\'s action. See \ue200cite\ue20217†WFP Version-Independent Names and Targeting Specific Versions of Windows\ue201 for more information.\\nL116: #### Examples\\nL117: The following C++ example shows how to initialize and add a filter using FwpmFilterAdd0 that\\nL118: specifically blocks traffic on IP V4 for all applications.\\nL119: \\nL120:     `\\nL121:     // Add filter to block traffic on IP V4 for all applications.\\nL122:     //\\nL123:     FWPM_FILTER0      fwpFilter;\\nL124:     FWPM_SUBLAYER0    fwpFilterSubLayer;\\nL125: \\nL126:     RtlZeroMemory(&fwpFilter, sizeof(FWPM_FILTER0));\\nL127: \\nL128:     fwpFilter.layerKey = FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V4;\\nL129:     fwpFilter.action.type = FWP_ACTION_BLOCK;\\nL130:     if (&fwpFilterSubLayer.subLayerKey != NULL)\\nL131:         fwpFilter.subLayerKey = fwpFilterSubLayer.subLayerKey;\\nL132: \\nL133:     fwpFilter.weight.type = FWP_EMPTY; // auto-weight.\\nL134:     fwpFilter.numFilterConditions = 0; // this applies to all application traffic\\nL135:     fwpFilter.displayData.name = L\\"Receive/Accept Layer Block\\";\\nL136:     fwpFilter.displayData.description = L\\"Filter to block all inbound connections.\\";\\nL137: \\nL138:     printf(\\"Adding filter to block all inbound connections.\\\\n\\");\\nL139:     result = FwpmFilterAdd0(engineHandle, &fwpFilter, NULL, NULL);\\nL140: \\nL141:     if (result != ERROR_SUCCESS)\\nL142:         printf(\\"FwpmFilterAdd0 failed. Syntax\\nL34: \\nL35:     `typedef struct FWPM_SESSION0_ {\\nL36:       GUID               sessionKey;\\nL37:       FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 displayData;\\nL38:       UINT32             flags;\\nL39:       UINT32             txnWaitTimeoutInMSec;\\nL40:       DWORD              processId;\\nL41:       SID                *sid;\\nL42:       wchar_t            *username;\\nL43:       BOOL               kernelMode;\\nL44:     } FWPM_SESSION0;\\nL45:     `\\nL46: ## Members\\nL47: \\nL48: `sessionKey`\\nL49: \\nL50: Uniquely identifies the session.\\nL51: \\nL52: If this member is zero in the call to \ue200cite\ue2025†FwpmEngineOpen0\ue201 , Base Filtering Engine (BFE) will generate a GUID.\\nL53: \\nL54: `displayData`\\nL55: \\nL56: Allows sessions to be annotated in a human-readable form.\\nL57: \\nL58: See \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0\ue201 for more information.\\nL59: \\nL60: `flags`\\nL61: \\nL62: Settings to control session behavior.\\nL63: \\nL64: Session flag  | Meaning\\nL65: --- | ---\\nL66: FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC\\nL67:  | When this flag is set, any objects added during the session are automatically deleted when the session ends.\\nL68: \\nL69: FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_RESERVED\\nL70:  | Reserved.\\nL71: \\nL72: `txnWaitTimeoutInMSec`\\nL73: \\nL74: Time in milli-seconds that a client will wait to begin a transaction.\\nL75: \\nL76: If this member is zero, BFE will use a default timeout.\\nL77: \\nL78: `processId`\\nL79: \\nL80: Process ID of the client.\\nL81: \\nL82: `sid`\\nL83: \\nL84: SID of the client.\\nL85: \\nL86: `username`\\nL87: \\nL88: User name of the client.\\nL89: \\nL90: `kernelMode`\\nL91: \\nL92: TRUE if this is a kernel-mode client.\\nL93: ## Remarks\\nL94: \\nL95: This structure contains information supplied by the client when creating a session by calling \ue200cite\ue2025†FwpmEngineOpen0\ue201 , or information retrieved from the system when enumerating sessions by calling \ue200cite\ue2027†FwpmSessionEnum0\ue201 .\\nL96: \\nL97: The members processId, sid, username, and kernelMode are not supplied by the client. They are supplied by BFE and can be retrieved when enumerating sessions.\\nL98: FWPM_SESSION0 is a specific implementation of FWPM_SESSION. See \ue200cite\ue2028†WFP Version-Independent Names and Targeting Specific Versions of Windows\ue201 for more information.\\nL99: ## Requirements\\nL100: \\nL101: Requirement  | Value\\nL102: --- | ---\\nL103: Minimum supported client  | Windows\xa0Vista [desktop apps only]\\nL104: Minimum supported server  | Windows Server\xa02008 [desktop apps only]\\nL105: Header  | fwpmtypes.h\\nL106: \\nL107: ## See also\\nL108: \\nL109: \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0\ue201 L110: \\nL111: \ue200cite\ue2025†FwpmEngineOpen0\ue201 L112: \\nL113: \ue200cite\ue2027†FwpmSessionEnum0\ue201 L114: \\nL115: \ue200cite\ue2029†Windows Filtering Platform API Structures\ue201 L116: \\nL117: * * *\\nL118: ## Feedback\\nL119: \\nL120: Was this page helpful?\\nL121: \\nL122: Yes No No\\nL123: \\nL124: Need help with this topic?\\nL125: \\nL126: Want to try using Ask Learn to clarify or guide you through this topic?\\nL127: \\nL128: Ask Learn Ask Learn\\nL129: \\nL130: Suggest a fix?\\nL131: \\nL132: * * *\\nL133: \\nL134: ## Additional resources\\nL135: \\nL136: * * *\\nL137: \\nL138:   * Last updated on 2021-04-02\\nL139: \\nL140: ### In this article\\nL141: \\nL142: Was this page helpful?\\nL143: \\nL144: Need help with this topic?\\nL145: \\nL146: Want to try using Ask Learn to clarify or guide you through this topic?\\nL147: \\nL148: Ask Learn Ask Learn\\nL149: \\nL150: Suggest a fix?\\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\nAccess control (Windows Filtering Platform) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/access-control)\\n\ue200cite\ue202turn25view3\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; You can try changing directories.\\nL24: # Access control (Windows Filtering Platform)\\nL25: \\nL26: Feedback\\nL27: \\nL28: Summarize this article for me\\nL29: \\nL30: ## In this article\\nL31: \\nL32: In Windows Filtering Platform (WFP), the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) service implements the standard \ue200cite\ue2025†Windows access control model\ue201 based on access tokens and security descriptors.\\nL33: ## Access control model\\nL34: \\nL35: Security descriptors can be specified when adding new WFP objects, such as filters and sub-layers. Security descriptors are managed using the WFP management functions Fwpm*GetSecurityInfo0 and Fwpm*SetSecurityInfo0, where * stands for the WFP object\'s name. These functions are semantically identical to the Windows \ue200cite\ue2026†GetSecurityInfo\ue201 and \ue200cite\ue2027†SetSecurityInfo\ue201 functions.\\nL36: \\nL37: Note\\nL38: \\nL39: The Fwpm*SetSecurityInfo0 functions cannot be called from within an explicit transaction.\\nL40: \\nL41: Note\\nL42: The Fwpm*SetSecurityInfo0 functions can only be called from within a dynamic session if they are being used to manage a dynamic object created within the same session.\\nL43: \\nL44: The default security descriptor for the filter engine (the root Engine object in the diagram below) is as follows.\\nL45:   * Grant GENERIC_ALL (GA) access rights to the built-in Administrators group.\\nL46:   * Grant GENERIC_READ (GR) GENERIC_WRITE (GW) GENERIC_EXECUTE (GX) access rights to network configuration operators.\\nL47:   * Grant GRGWGX access rights to the following service security identifiers (SSIDs): MpsSvc (Windows Firewall), NapAgent (Network Access Protection Agent), PolicyAgent (IPsec Policy Agent), RpcSs (Remote Procedure Call), and WdiServiceHost (Diagnostic Service Host).\\nL48:   * Grant FWPM_ACTRL_OPEN and FWPM_ACTRL_CLASSIFY to everyone. (These are WFP-specific access rights, described in table below.)\\nL49: The remaining default security descriptors are derived through inheritance.\\nL50: There are some access checks, such as for Fwpm*Add0, Fwpm*CreateEnumHandle0, Fwpm*SubscribeChanges0 function calls, that cannot be done at the individual object level. For these functions, there are container objects for each object type. For the standard object types (for example, providers, callouts, filters), the existing Fwpm*GetSecurityInfo0 and Fwpm*SetSecurityInfo0 functions are overloaded, such that a null GUID parameter identifies the associated container.\\nL51: For the other object types (for example, network events and IPsec security associations), there are explicit functions for managing the container\'s security information.\\nL52: BFE supports automatic inheritance of Discretionary Access Control List (DACL) access control entries (ACEs). BFE does not support System Access Control List (SACL) ACEs. Objects inherit ACEs from their container. Containers inherit ACEs from the filter engine. The propagation paths are shown in the diagram below.\\nL53: \\nL54: \ue200cite\ue2028†Image: Diagram that shows the ACE propagation paths, starting with \'Engine\'.\ue201 L55: For the standard object types, BFE enforces all the generic and standard access rights. In addition, WFP defines the following specific access rights.\\nL56: WFP Access right  | Description\\nL57: --- | ---\\nL58: FWPM_ACTRL_ADD\\nL59:  | Required to add an object to a container.\\nL60: FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\\nL61:  | Required to create an association to an object. For example, to add a filter that references a callout, the caller must have ADD_LINK access to the callout.\\nL62: FWPM_ACTRL_BEGIN_READ_TXN\\nL63:  | Required to begin an explicit read transaction.\\nL64: FWPM_ACTRL_BEGIN_WRITE_TXN\\nL65:  | Required to begin an explicit write transaction.\\nL66: FWPM_ACTRL_CLASSIFY\\nL67:  | Required to classify against a user-mode layer.\\nL68: FWPM_ACTRL_ENUM\\nL69:  | Required to enumerate the objects in a container. However, the enumerator only returns objects to which the caller has FWPM_ACTRL_READ access.\\nL70: FWPM_ACTRL_OPEN\\nL71:  | Required to open a session with BFE.\\nL72: FWPM_ACTRL_READ\\nL73:  | Required to read an object\'s properties.\\nL74: FWPM_ACTRL_READ_STATS\\nL75:  | Required to read statistics.\\nL76: FWPM_ACTRL_SUBSCRIBE\\nL77:  | Required to subscribe for notifications. Subscribers will only receive notifications for objects to which they have FWPM_ACTRL_READ access.\\nL78: FWPM_ACTRL_WRITE\\nL79:  | Required to set engine options.\\nL80: BFE skips all access checks for kernel-mode callers.\\nL81: \\nL82: In order to prevent administrators from locking themselves out of BFE, memb…2680 tokens truncated…lities\\n  6. Case 8: Debugging Past Drop - UWP app connects to Internet target address with all capabilities\\nShow 7 more\\n\\nThis document is intended to help network admins, support engineers, and developers to investigate UWP app network connectivity issues.\\n\\nThis document guides you through steps to debug Universal Windows Platform (UWP) app network connectivity issues by providing practical examples.\\n\\n## Typical causes of connectivity issues\\n\\nUWP app network connectivity issues are typically caused by:\\n\\n  1. The UWP applications not being permitted to receive loopback traffic. This permission must be configured. By default, UWP applications aren\'t allowed to receive loopback traffic\\n  2. The UWP app is missing the proper capability tokens\\n  3. The private range is configured incorrectly. For example, the private range is set incorrectly through GP/MDM policies, etc.\\n\\nTo understand these causes more thoroughly, there are several concepts to review.\\n\\nThe traffic of network packets (what\'s permitted and what\'s not) on Windows is determined by the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP). \\n## Debugging UWP App Loopback scenarios\\n\\nIf you need to establish a TCP/IP connection between two processes on the same host where one of them is a UWP app, you must enable loopback.\\n\\nTo enable loopback for client outbound connections, run the following command at a command prompt:\\n\\nWindows Command Prompt\\n\\nCopy\\n    \\n    `CheckNetIsolation.exe LoopbackExempt -a -n=<AppContainer or Package Family>\\n    `\\n\\nTo enable loopback for server inbound connections, run the following command at a command prompt:\\n\\nWindows Command Prompt\\n\\nCopy\\n    \\n    `CheckNetIsolation.exe LoopbackExempt -is -n=<AppContainer or Package Family>\\n    `\\n\\nYou can ensure loopback is enabled by checking the appx manifests of both the sender and receiver.\\n\\nFor more information about loopback scenarios, see Communicating with localhost (loopback).\\n\\nNote\\n\\nIf you are in the middle of developing a UWA application and want to test its loopback, ensure to uninstall and re-install the UWA app if the network capabilities change for whatever reason.\\n\\nAlso, see How to enable loopback and troubleshoot network isolation (Windows Runtime apps).\\n\\n## Debugging Live Drops\\n\\nIf the issue happened recently, but you find you aren\'t able to reproduce the issue, go to Debugging Past Drops for the appropriate trace commands.\\n\\nIf you can consistently reproduce the issue, then you can run the following command in an admin command prompt to gather a fresh trace:\\n\\nConsole\\n\\nCopy\\n    \\n    `Netsh wfp capture start keywords=19\\n    <Run UWP app>\\n    Netsh wfp capture stop\\n    `\\n\\nThese commands generate a wfpdiag.cab. Inside the .cab exists a wfpdiag.xml, which contains any allow or drop netEvents and filters that existed during that repro. Without \\"keywords=19\\", the trace will only collect drop netEvents.\\n\\nInside the wfpdiag.xml, search for netEvents that have FWPM_NET_EVENT_TYPE_CLASSIFY_DROP as the netEvent type. To find the relevant drop events, search for the drop events with matching destination IP address, package SID, or application ID name. The characters in the application ID name will be separated by periods:\\n\\nXML\\n\\nCopy\\n    \\n    `(ex)\\n    \\n    <asString>\\n    \\\\\\\\.d.e.v.i.c.e.\\\\\\\\.h.a.r.d.d.i.s.k.v.o.l.u.m.e.1.\\\\\\\\.w.i.n.d.o.w.s.\\\\\\\\.s.y.s.t.e.m.3.2.\\\\\\\\.s.v.c.h.o.s.t...e.x.e...\\n    \\n    </asString>\\n    `\\n\\nThe netEvent will have more information about the packet that was dropped including information about its capabilities, the filter that dropped the packet, and much more.\\n\\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\nCan not connect to local port - Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/4247800/can-not-connect-to-local-port)\\n\ue200cite\ue202turn24search3\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Published: 5.3 years ago; Crawled: 2 months ago; Very strange port 135 responds and 7080 does not.Besides the Windows firewall, do you have any other third-party security solutions (antivirus or antimalware) running on your PC? ... Case 8: Debugging Past Drop - UWP app connects to Internet target address with all capabilities\nShow 7 more\n\nThis document is intended to help network admins, support engineers, and developers to investigate UWP app network connectivity issues.\n\nThis document guides you through steps to debug Universal Windows Platform (UWP) app network connectivity issues by providing practical examples.\n\n## Typical causes of connectivity issues\n\nUWP app network connectivity issues are typically caused by:\n\n  1. The UWP applications not being permitted to receive loopback traffic. This permission must be configured. By default, UWP applications aren\'t allowed to receive loopback traffic\n  2. The UWP app is missing the proper capability tokens\n  3. The private range is configured incorrectly. For example, the private range is set incorrectly through GP/MDM policies, etc.\n\nTo understand these causes more thoroughly, there are several concepts to review.\n\nThe traffic of network packets (what\'s permitted and what\'s not) on Windows is determined by the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP). When a UWP app or the private range is configured incorrectly, it affects how the UWP app\'s network traffic will be processed by WFP.\n\nWhen a packet is processed by WFP, the characteristics of that packet must explicitly match all the conditions of a filter to either be permitted or dropped to its target address. Connectivity issues typically happen when the packet doesn\'t match any of the filter conditions, leading the packet to be dropped by a default block filter. The presence of the default block filters ensures network isolation for UWP applications. Specifically, it guarantees a network drop for a packet that doesn\'t have the correct capabilities for the resource it\'s trying to reach. Such a packet drop ensures the application\'s granular access to each resource type and preventing the application from escaping its environment.\n\nFor more information on the filter arbitration algorithm and network isolation, see Filter Arbitration and Isolation.\n\nThe following sections cover debugging case examples for loopback and non-loopback UWP app network connectivity issues.\n\n## Debugging UWP App Loopback scenarios\n\nIf you need to establish a TCP/IP connection between two processes on the same host where one of them is a UWP app, you must enable loopback.\n\nTo enable loopback for client outbound connections, run the following command at a command prompt:\n\nWindows Command Prompt\n\nCopy\n    \n    `CheckNetIsolation.exe LoopbackExempt -a -n=<AppContainer or Package Family>\n    `\n\nTo enable loopback for server inbound connections, run the following command at a command prompt:\n\nWindows Command Prompt\n\nCopy\n    \n    `CheckNetIsolation.exe LoopbackExempt -is -n=<AppContainer or Package Family>\n    `\n\nYou can ensure loopback is enabled by checking the appx manifests of both the sender and receiver.\n\nFor more information about loopback scenarios, see Communicating with localhost (loopback).\n\nNote\n\nIf you are in the middle of developing a UWA application and want to test its loopback, ensure to uninstall and re-install the UWA app if the network capabilities change for whatever reason.\n\nAlso, see How to enable loopback and troubleshoot network isolation (Windows Runtime apps).\n\n## Debugging Live Drops\n\nIf the issue happened recently, but you find you aren\'t able to reproduce the issue, go to Debugging Past Drops for the appropriate trace commands.\n\nIf you can consistently reproduce the issue, then you can run the following command in an admin command prompt to gather a fresh trace:\n\nConsole\n\nCopy\n    \n    `Netsh wfp capture start keywords=19\n    <Run UWP app>\n    Netsh wfp capture stop\n    `\n\nThese commands generate a wfpdiag.cab. The ALG FTP plug-in supports these sessions by redirecting all traffic that meets the following criteria to a private listening port in the range of 3000 to 5000 on the loopback adapter: ... 67  | UDP  | DHCP Server  | Internet Connection Firewall/Internet Connection Sharing\nThe following settings are LDAP session options:\n\n  * PingKeepAliveTimeout = 120 seconds (how long it waits after last response from server before it starts sending ping)\n  * PingLimit = 4 (how many pings are sent before connection is closed)\n  * PingWaitTimeout = 2000 ms (how long it waits for the ICMP response)\n  * Reference: LdapSessionOptions Class\n\n### Application Layer Gateway service\n\nThis subcomponent of the Internet Connection Sharing/Internet Connection Firewall (ICF) service provides support for plug-ins that allow network protocols to pass through the firewall and work behind Internet Connection Sharing. Application Layer Gateway (ALG) plug-ins can open ports and change data (such as ports and IP addresses) that are embedded in packets. FTP is the only network protocol that has a plug-in that is included with Windows Server. The ALG FTP plug-in supports active FTP sessions through the network address translation (NAT) engine that these components use. The ALG FTP plug-in supports these sessions by redirecting all traffic that meets the following criteria to a private listening port in the range of 3000 to 5000 on the loopback adapter:\n\n  * Passes through the NAT engine\n  * Is directed toward port 21\n\nThe ALG FTP plug-in then monitors and updates FTP control channel traffic so that the FTP plug-in can forward port mappings through the NAT for the FTP data channels. Please tell me why it is dynamically allowed by firewall.....\n\nMicrosoft Security | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Entra ID\n\nMicrosoft Security | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Entra ID\n\nAnswer accepted by question author\n\nImage\n\nSiva-kumar-selvaraj •\n\n[Button: Follow ]\n\n15,741 Reputation points • Volunteer Moderator\n\nMar 21, 2022, 12:54 AM\n\nHello @tarou chabi ,\n\nThanks for reaching out.\n\nFrom your query, I understand that you would like to know how Azure AD handles localhost ("https://localhost") as response URL while issuing SAML token when you have blocked 443 inbound in the firewall, please correct me if I\'m wrong here?\n\nIf you have configured application with Azure AD for SSO with response URL as "https://localhost" then Azure AD send SAML token in body using HTTP POST call to the localhost (current device) then your application consumes this token through network services that are running on the host via the loopback network interface. Route Nullifying\n     * Use routing rules to blackhole traffic to `127.0.0.1`.\n       * On Linux:\n\nBash\n\nCopy\n            \n            `       sudo ip route add blackhole 127.0.0.1\n            `\n\n       * On Windows:\n\nWindows Command Prompt\n\nCopy\n            \n            `       route add 127.0.0.1 MASK 255.255.255.255 0.0.0.0\n            `\n\nImportant Considerations:\n\n  * System Impact: Completely disabling or misconfiguring the loopback IP can disrupt internal services and applications relying on `127.0.0.1`. I changed the server to listen on the real IP addresss of the adapter and ran the client on another machine and the firewall on the client machine had to be turned off as well (!!!)\n\n# Strange firewall behaviour\n\nEuroEager2008 171 Reputation points\n\n2020-11-17T16:56:08.33+00:00\n\nI made the simplest ftp server by TcpListener (.net 5), listening at port 21 on the loopback address, opened tcp port 21 in case that should metter on a loopback connection.\nTested by another console by telnet (127.0.0.1 21) and sending "manually" active ftp commands like USER, PASS, CWD and TYPE, all works fine until the telnet client sends PORT followed by space and some numbers according to protocol, then the server hit an IOException stating that connection was closed by the client.\n(PORT has to be followed by at least one space to fail).\n\nAfter struggling around I was hinted by a colleague to turn off the windows firewall and voila, working fine.\n\nI changed the server to listen on the real IP addresss of the adapter and ran the client on another machine and the firewall on the client machine had to be turned off as well (!!!)\n\nPlease note that using another port than 21 fixes the problem even with the firewalls turned on.\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nQuarantine Behavior | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/mt-mt/windows/security/operating-system-security/network-security/windows-firewall/quarantine)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn26search10\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Published: 1.5 years ago; Crawled: 5 months ago; To counter the potential exploitation, Windows Firewall quarantines an interface until the system successfully recategorizes the network, and Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) has the correct filters applied for the updated interface configuration. ... The quarantine default inbound block filter blocks any new nonloopback inbound connections, unless the packet isn\'t explicitly permitted by another filter in the quarantine sublayer.\nDuring quarantine, all new inbound connections without exceptions are blocked.\n\nThis document describes the quarantine feature and explains why the application traffic could be blocked by quarantine.\n\n## Quarantine filters\n\nThe quarantine feature creates filters that can be split into three categories:\n\n  * Quarantine default inbound block filter\n  * Quarantine default exception filters\n  * Interface unquarantine filters\n\nThese filters are added in the `FWPM_SUBLAYER_MPSSVC_QUARANTINE` sublayer and these layers are:\n\n  1. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V4`\n  2. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V6`\n  3. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V4`\n  4. `FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V6`\n\nNote\n\nAny firewall rules added by policy settings don\'t affect the filters in the quarantine sublayer. Filters from firewall rules are added in the `FWPM_SUBLAYER_MPSSVC_WF` sublayer. In other words, you can\'t add your own exception filters to prevent packets from being evaluated by quarantine filters.\n\nFor more information about WFP layers and sublayers, see WFP Operation.\n\n### Quarantine default inbound block filter\n\nThe quarantine default inbound block filter blocks any new nonloopback inbound connections, unless the packet isn\'t explicitly permitted by another filter in the quarantine sublayer.\n\n### Quarantine default exception filters\n\nWhen the interface is in quarantine state, the quarantine default exception filters permit new inbound connections given that they meet the conditions of an exception filter. One example of the exception filters is the quarantine default inbound loopback exception filter. This exception filter allows all loopback packets when the interface is in quarantine state.\n\n### Interface unquarantine filter\n\nThe interface unquarantine filters allow all nonloopback packets if the interface is successfully categorized.\n\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nConnections to loopback adresses do not work - Microsoft Q&A (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/4273951/connections-to-loopback-adresses-do-not-work)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn26search11\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Published: 4.0 years ago; Crawled: 3 days ago; Allow Microsoft Edge to access the network in your firewall or antivirus settings. ... https://learn-attachment.microsoft.com/api/attachments/1430b2b7-d315-4b0f-9f95-8f2243b2545c? ... See also\n\nThe Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) filtering condition flags are each represented by a bitfield.\n\nThese flags and the filtering layers where they can be used are defined as follows.\n\nFWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_LOOPBACK\n\n    \n\nTests whether the network traffic is loopback traffic.\n\nFiltering layers:\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_IPPACKET_V{4|6}\n\n  * Server 2008, Windows Vista with SP1, and later.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_ICMP_ERROR_V{4|6}\n\nPoznámka:\n\nAvailable only on Windows Server 2008, Windows Vista with SP1, and later.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_OUTBOUND_ICMP_ERROR_V{4|6}\n\nPoznámka:\n\nAvailable only on Windows Server 2008, Windows Vista with SP1, and later.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_APPCONTAINER_LOOPBACK\n\n# 条件フラグのフィルター処理\n\nフィードバック\n\n## この記事の内容\n\n  1. 必要条件\n  2. 関連項目\n\nWindows フィルタリング プラットフォーム (WFP) フィルター条件フラグは、それぞれビットフィールドで表されます。\n\nこれらのフラグと使用できるフィルター レイヤーは、次のように定義されます。\n\nFWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_LOOPBACK\n\n    \n\nネットワーク トラフィックがループバック トラフィックであるかどうかをテストします。\n\nレイヤーのフィルター処理:\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_IPPACKET_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_OUTBOUND_IPPACKET_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_TRANSPORT_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_OUTBOUND_TRANSPORT_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_STREAM_{V4|6}\n\nNote\n\nWindows Server 2008、WINDOWS Vista SP1 以降でのみ使用できます。\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_ICMP_ERROR_V{4|6}\n\nNote\n\nWindows Server 2008、WINDOWS Vista SP1 以降でのみ使用できます。\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_OUTBOUND_ICMP_ERROR_V{4|6}\n\nNote\n\nWindows Server 2008、WINDOWS Vista SP1 以降でのみ使用できます。\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V{4|6}\n\nNote\n\nWindows Server 2008、WINDOWS Vista SP1 以降でのみ使用できます。\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_FLOW_ESTABLISHED_V{4|6}\n\nNote\n\nWindows Server 2008、WINDOWS Vista SP1 以降でのみ使用できます。\n\nFWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_IPSEC_SECURED\n\n    \n\nネットワーク トラフィックが IPsec によって保護されているかどうかをテストします。\n\nレイヤーのフィルター処理:\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_IPPACKET_V{4|6}\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_TRANSPORT_V{4|6}\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V{4|6}\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V{4|6}\n\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nIndicateurs de condition de filtrage (Fwptypes.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/fr-fr/windows/win32/fwp/filtering-condition-flags-)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn27search5\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 2 weeks ago; FWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_LOOPBACK ... FWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_APPCONTAINER_LOOPBACK\n\n# 조건 플래그 필터링\n\n피드백\n\n## 이 문서의 내용\n\n  1. 요구 사항\n  2. 추가 정보\n\nWFP(Windows 필터링 플랫폼) 필터링 조건 플래그는 각각 비트필드로 표시됩니다.\n\n이러한 플래그 및 사용할 수 있는 필터링 계층은 다음과 같이 정의됩니다.\n\nFWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_LOOPBACK\n\n    \n\n네트워크 트래픽이 루프백 트래픽인지 테스트합니다.\n\n레이어 필터링:\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_IPPACKET_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_OUTBOUND_IPPACKET_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_TRANSPORT_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_OUTBOUND_TRANSPORT_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_STREAM_{V4|6}\n\n참고 항목\n\nWindows Server 2008, Windows Vista SP1 이상에서만 사용할 수 있습니다.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_ICMP_ERROR_V{4|6}\n\n참고 항목\n\nWindows Server 2008, Windows Vista SP1 이상에서만 사용할 수 있습니다.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_OUTBOUND_ICMP_ERROR_V{4|6}\n\n참고 항목\n\nWindows Server 2008, Windows Vista SP1 이상에서만 사용할 수 있습니다.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V{4|6}\n\n참고 항목\n\nWindows Server 2008, Windows Vista SP1 이상에서만 사용할 수 있습니다.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_FLOW_ESTABLISHED_V{4|6}\n\n참고 항목\n\nWindows Server 2008, Windows Vista SP1 이상에서만 사용할 수 있습니다.\n\nFWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_IPSEC_SECURED\n\n    \n\n네트워크 트래픽이 IPsec에 의해 보호되는지 테스트합니다.\n\n레이어 필터링:\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_IPPACKET_V{4|6}\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_TRANSPORT_V{4|6}\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V{4|6}\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V{4|6}\n\nFWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_REAUTHORIZE\n\n    \n\n새 연결이 아닌 정책 변경에 대한 테스트입니다.\n\n레이어 필터링:\n\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nFlag di condizione di filtro (Fwptypes.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/it-it/windows/win32/fwp/filtering-condition-flags-)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn27search9\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Published: 3.3 years ago; Crawled: 3 months ago; FWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_LOOPBACK ... FWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_APPCONTAINER_LOOPBACK\n\n# Flag di condizione di filtro\n\nCommenti e suggerimenti\n\n## In questo articolo\n\nI flag di condizione di filtro di Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) sono rappresentati da un campo bit.\n\nQuesti flag e i livelli di filtro in cui possono essere usati sono definiti come segue.\n\nFWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_LOOPBACK\n\n    \n\nVerifica se il traffico di rete è il traffico di loopback.\n\nFiltri dei livelli:\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_IPPACKET_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_OUTBOUND_IPPACKET_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_TRANSPORT_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_OUTBOUND_TRANSPORT_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_STREAM_{V4|6}\n\nNota\n\nDisponibile solo in Windows Server 2008, Windows Vista con SP1 e versioni successive.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_ICMP_ERROR_V{4|6}\n\nNota\n\nDisponibile solo in Windows Server 2008, Windows Vista con SP1 e versioni successive.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_OUTBOUND_ICMP_ERROR_V{4|6}\n\nNota\n\nDisponibile solo in Windows Server 2008, Windows Vista con SP1 e versioni successive.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V{4|6}\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V{4|6}\n\nNota\n\nDisponibile solo in Windows Server 2008, Windows Vista con SP1 e versioni successive.\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_FLOW_ESTABLISHED_V{4|6}\n\nNota\n\nDisponibile solo in Windows Server 2008, Windows Vista con SP1 e versioni successive.\n\nFWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_IPSEC_SECURED\n\n    \n\nVerifica se il traffico di rete è protetto da IPsec.\n\nFiltri dei livelli:\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_IPPACKET_V{4|6}\n  * FWPM_LAYER_INBOUND_TRANSPORT_V{4|6}\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V{4|6}\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V{4|6}\n\nFWP_CONDITION_FLAG_IS_REAUTHORIZE\n\n    \n\nVerifica una modifica dei criteri anziché una nuova connessione.\n\nFiltri dei livelli:\n\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V{4|6}\n  * FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V{4|6}\n\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n筛选条件标志 (Fwptypes.h) -
