You can try changing directories.\\nL24: # FWPM_FILTER0 structure (fwpmtypes.h)\\nL25: \\nL26: Feedback\\nL27: \\nL28: Summarize this article for me\\nL29: \\nL30: ## In this article\\nL31: \\nL32: The FWPM_FILTER0 structure stores the state associated with a filter.\\nL33: ## Syntax\\nL34: \\nL35:     `typedef struct FWPM_FILTER0_ {\\nL36:       GUID                   filterKey;\\nL37:       FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0     displayData;\\nL38:       UINT32                 flags;\\nL39:       GUID                   *providerKey;\\nL40:       FWP_BYTE_BLOB          providerData;\\nL41:       GUID                   layerKey;\\nL42:       GUID                   subLayerKey;\\nL43:       FWP_VALUE0             weight;\\nL44:       UINT32                 numFilterConditions;\\nL45:       FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0 *filterCondition;\\nL46:       FWPM_ACTION0           action;\\nL47:       union {\\nL48:         UINT64 rawContext;\\nL49:         GUID   providerContextKey;\\nL50:       };\\nL51:       GUID                   *reserved;\\nL52:       UINT64                 filterId;\\nL53:       FWP_VALUE0             effectiveWeight;\\nL54:     } FWPM_FILTER0;\\nL55:     `\\nL56: ## Members\\nL57: \\nL58: `filterKey`\\nL59: \\nL60: Uniquely identifies the session.\\nL61: \\nL62: If the GUID is initialized to zero in the call to \ue200cite\ue2025†FwpmFilterAdd0\ue201 , the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) will generate one.\\nL63: \\nL64: `displayData`\\nL65: \\nL66: A \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0\ue201 structure that contains human-readable annotations associated with the filter. The name member of the FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 structure is required.\\nL67: \\nL68: `flags`\\nL69: \\nL70: A combination of the following values.\\nL71: \\nL72: Filter flag  | Meaning\\nL73: --- | ---\\nL74: \\nL75: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_NONE**\\nL76:  | Default.\\nL77: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_PERSISTENT**\\nL78:  | Filter is persistent, that is, it survives across BFE stop/start. **Note**\xa0\xa0This flag cannot be set together with **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_BOOTTIME**.\\nL79: \\nL80: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_BOOTTIME**\\nL81:  | Filter is enforced at boot-time, even before BFE starts. **Note**\xa0\xa0This flag cannot be set together with **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_PERSISTENT**.\\nL82: \\nL83: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_HAS_PROVIDER_CONTEXT**\\nL84:  | Filter references a provider context.\\nL85: \\nL86: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHT**\\nL87:  | Clear filter action right.\\nL88: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_PERMIT_IF_CALLOUT_UNREGISTERED**\\nL89:  | If the callout is not registered, the filter is treated as a permit filter. **Note**\xa0\xa0This flag can be set only if the **action** type is **FWP_ACTION_CALLOUT_TERMINATING** or **FWP_ACTION_CALLOUT_UNKNOWN**.\\nL90: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_DISABLED**\\nL91:  | Filter is disabled. A provider\'s filters are disabled when the BFE starts if the provider has no associated Windows service name, or if the associated service is not set to auto-start. **Note**\xa0\xa0This flag cannot be set when adding new filters. It can only be returned by BFE when getting or enumerating filters.\\nL92: **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_INDEXED**\\nL93:  | Filter is indexed to help enable faster lookup during classification. **Note**\xa0\xa0Available only in Windows\xa08 and Windows Server\xa02012.\\nL94: \\nL95: `providerKey`\\nL96: \\nL97: Optional GUID of the policy provider that manages this filter. See \ue200cite\ue2027†Built-in Provider Identifiers\ue201 for a list of predefined policy providers.\\nL98: \\nL99: `providerData`\\nL100: \\nL101: A \ue200cite\ue2028†FWP_BYTE_BLOB\ue201 structure that contains optional provider-specific data used by providers to store additional context information with the object.\\nL102: \\nL103: `layerKey`\\nL104: GUID of the layer where the filter resides. See \ue200cite\ue2029†Filtering Layer Identifiers\ue201 for a list of possible values.\\nL105: \\nL106: `subLayerKey`\\nL107: \\nL108: GUID of the sub-layer where the filter resides. See \ue200cite\ue20210†Filtering Sub-Layer Identifiers\ue201 for a list of built-in sub-layers.\\nL109: \\nL110: If this is set to IID_NULL, the filter is added to the default sublayer.\\nL111: \\nL112: `weight`\\nL113: A \ue200cite\ue20211†FWP_VALUE0\ue201 structure that specifies the weight of the filter. The weight indicates the priority of the filter, where higher-numbered weights have higher priorities (and will be evaluated before lower-weighted filters).\\nL114: \\nL115: Possible type values for weight are as follows.\\nL116: \\nL117: **weight** type  | Meaning\\nL118: --- | ---\\nL119: \\nL120: **FWP_UINT64**\\nL121:  | BFE will use the supplied value as the filter\'s weight.\\nL122: **FWP_UINT8**\\nL123: 0–15\\nL124:  | BFE will use the supplied value as a weight range index and will compute the filter\'s weight in that range. See \ue200cite\ue20212†Filter Weight Assignment\ue201 for more information.\\nL125: \\nL126: **FWP_EMPTY**\\nL127:  | BFE will automatically assign a weight based on the filter conditions.\\nL128: \\nL129: See \ue200cite\ue20213†Filter Weight Identifiers\ue201 for built-in constants that may be used to compute the filter weight.\\nL130: \\nL131: `numFilterConditions`\\nL132: \\nL133: Number of filter conditions.\\nL134: \\nL135: `filterCondition`\\nL136: Array of \ue200cite\ue20214†FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0\ue201 structures that contain all the filtering conditions. All must be true for the action to be performed. In other words, the conditions are evaluated using the AND operator. If no conditions are specified, the action is always performed.\\nL137: \\nL138: **Note**\xa0\xa0In Windows\xa07 and Windows Server\xa02008\xa0R2, consecutive conditions with the same fieldKey will be evaluated using the OR operator.\\nL139: \\nL140: \\nL141: \\nL142: `action`\\nL143: A \ue200cite\ue20215†FWPM_ACTION0\ue201 structure that specifies the action to be performed if all the filter conditions are true.\\nL144: \\nL145: `rawContext`\\nL146: \\nL147: Available when the filter does not have provider context information, that is, flags does not contain FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_HAS_PROVIDER_CONTEXT. See \ue200cite\ue20216†Filter Context Identifiers\ue201 for a list of built-in possible values.\\nL148: \\nL149: The rawContext is placed \'as is\' in the context member of the corresponding FWPS_FILTER0 structure, which is documented in the WDK.\\nL150: \\nL151: `providerContextKey`\\nL152: Available when the filter has provider context information, that is, flags contains FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_HAS_PROVIDER_CONTEXT. See \ue200cite\ue20217†Built-in Provider Context Identifiers\ue201 for a list of predefined policy provider contexts.\\nL153: \\nL154: The LUID of the provider context specified by the providerContextKey is used to fill in the context member of the corresponding FWPS_FILTER0 structure, which is documented in the WDK.\\nL155: \\nL156: `reserved`\\nL157: \\nL158: Reserved for system use.\\nL159: \\nL160: `filterId`\\nL161: LUID identifying the filter. This is also the LUID of the corresponding FWPS_FILTER0 structure, which is documented in the WDK.\\nL162: \\nL163: `effectiveWeight`\\nL164: \\nL165: An \ue200cite\ue20211†FWP_VALUE0\ue201 structure that contains the weight assigned to FWPS_FILTER0, which is documented in the WDK.\\nL166: ## Remarks\\nL167: \\nL168: The first ten members of this structure contain information supplied when adding objects.\\nL169: \\nL170: The last members, filterId and effectiveWeight, provides additional information when getting/enumerating objects.\\nL171: \\nL172: FWPM_FILTER0 is a specific implementation of FWPM_FILTER. See \ue200cite\ue20218†WFP Version-Independent Names and Targeting Specific Versions of Windows\ue201 for more information.\\nL173: ## Requirements\\nL174: \\nL175: Requirement  | Value\\nL176: --- | ---\\nL177: Minimum supported client  | Windows\xa0Vista [desktop apps only]\\nL178: Minimum supported server  | Windows Server\xa02008 [desktop apps only]\\nL179: Header  | fwpmtypes.h\\nL180: \\nL181: ## 本轮新增证据是：6.1.1受支持CLI能力边界、实际loopback监听关系、当前权限结果，以及WFP对loopback可过滤/动态恢复/程序身份/访问控制的一手API依据。生产实现继续冻结；当前失败是网络设施前置未成立，没有产品修复范围。\n+\n+## 7. 按root追加要求：无驱动C#辅助设施的最小实现合同 v4.1\n+\n+**可以用本机普通C#编译和系统DLL实现；本轮未编译或执行它。**本轮只读确认本机存在 `C:/Windows/Microsoft.NET/Framework64/v4.0.30319/csc.exe`（4.8.9221.0），当前进程X64，PowerShell有Add-Type；未发现本机Windows Kits/10/Include目录。因此不需要下载编译器、NuGet包或驱动，但实现者仍须正确处理原生结构体ABI。以下只是设计文档内的声明合同，没有Main或API调用，不是运行工具。\n+\n+### 7.1 最窄P/Invoke声明\n+\n+```csharp\n+using System;\n+using System.Runtime.InteropServices;\n+\n+internal static class WfpNative {\n+    [DllImport(\"Fwpuclnt.dll\", ExactSpelling = true)]\n+    internal static extern uint FwpmEngineOpen0(IntPtr serverName,\n+        uint authnService, IntPtr authIdentity, IntPtr session,\n+        out IntPtr engineHandle);\n+    [DllImport(\"Fwpuclnt.dll\", ExactSpelling = true, CharSet = CharSet.Unicode)]\n+    internal static extern uint FwpmGetAppIdFromFileName0(string fileName,\n+        out IntPtr appId);\n+    [DllImport(\"Fwpuclnt.dll\", ExactSpelling = true)]\n+    internal static extern uint FwpmTransactionBegin0(IntPtr engineHandle, uint flags);\n+    [DllImport(\"Fwpuclnt.dll\", ExactSpelling = true)]\n+    internal static extern uint FwpmFilterAdd0(IntPtr engineHandle,\n+        IntPtr filter, IntPtr securityDescriptor, out ulong filterId);\n+    [DllImport(\"Fwpuclnt.dll\", ExactSpelling = true)]\n+    internal static extern uint FwpmTransactionCommit0(IntPtr engineHandle);\n+    [DllImport(\"Fwpuclnt.dll\", ExactSpelling = true)]\n+    internal static extern uint FwpmTransactionAbort0(IntPtr engineHandle);\n+    [DllImport(\"Fwpuclnt.dll\", ExactSpelling = true)]\n+    internal static extern uint FwpmEngineClose0(IntPtr engineHandle);\n+    [DllImport(\"Fwpuclnt.dll\", ExactSpelling = true)]\n+    internal static extern void FwpmFreeMemory0(ref IntPtr memory);\n+}\n+```\n+\n+管理函数返回DWORD错误码，逐次检查0/nonzero；不能用Marshal.GetLastWin32Error替代返回值。上述IntPtr是对明确原生结构的指针，不是省略ABI校验的许可。serverName/authIdentity使用NULL，authnService取官方RPC_C_AUTHN_WINNT，session必须为完整FWPM_SESSION0且flags=1（DYNAMIC）。AppId使用官方函数取得的FWP_BYTE_BLOB指针，不手工拼文件路径字节；最后按官方要求FwpmFreeMemory0释放。\n+\n+一手签名：[EngineOpen0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmengineopen0)、[GetAppIdFromFileName0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmgetappidfromfilename0)、[FilterAdd0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfilteradd0)。EngineOpen0文档明确进程结束自动关闭会话；动态会话中的对象随结束自动删除，并非仅依赖正常finally执行。\n+\n+### 7.2 必要结构与过滤器内容\n+\n+| 原生类型 | 托管实现要点 | 本辅助工具实际使用 |\n+| --- | --- | --- |\n+| FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 | 两个UTF-16字符串指针 | 本题名称/说明，所有非托管字符串在添加完成前保持有效。 |\n+| FWPM_SESSION0 | Guid、displayData、uint flags/timeout/processId、SID/username指针、32位BOOL；按x64原生对齐 | 只填displayData和DYNAMIC，其余清零，不能用processId绑定被过滤进程。 |\n+| FWP_BYTE_BLOB | uint size + 对齐后的IntPtr data | 使用GetAppId函数分配的blob，不修改。 |\n+| FWP_VALUE0 / FWP_CONDITION_VALUE0 | 32位type + 原生union；x64指针union按8字节对齐 | weight取FWP_EMPTY；条件type=FWP_BYTE_BLOB_TYPE、union保存上述blob指针。 |\n+| FWPM_FILTER_CONDITION0 | Guid fieldKey、32位matchType、conditionValue | 唯一条件APP_ID / EQUAL / appBlob，避免多余endpoint限定。 |\n+| FWPM_ACTION0 | uint type + GUID union | type=FWP_ACTION_BLOCK（0x1001），其余清零，不用callout。 |\n+| FWPM_FILTER0 | 完整原生定义，尤其action后的16字节rawContext/providerContext union、reserved指针、filterId/effectiveWeight不能省略 | 两个不同filterKey；每个numFilterConditions=1；flags=0，无持久化/启动过滤；weight=EMPTY。 |\n+\n+最窄版可将subLayerKey置Guid.Empty，官方FWPM_FILTER0文档允许使用默认子层；无需额外provider、服务或callout注册。若实现选择本题独立子层，则只增加同一动态会话内的SubLayerAdd0，不改系统子层/ACL。两条过滤器在同一事务内全部成功才commit；任一失败abort并close，不能半启用IPv4或IPv6后继续测试。\n+\n+[FILTER_CONDITION0官方示例](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmtypes/ns-fwpmtypes-fwpm_filter_condition0)直接示范APP_ID + EQUAL + BYTE_BLOB；[FILTER0官方定义](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmtypes/ns-fwpmtypes-fwpm_filter0)给出完整布局、默认子层和自动权重。实现者应在任何BFE写调用之前核对Marshal.SizeOf/OffsetOf与原生x64布局，不能把32位示例偏移照搬到64位；先完成仅编译/布局检查，再由root决定管理员执行。\n+\n+本轮从微软维护的通用[Windows SDK头文件fwpmu.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/um/fwpmu.h)只读核对三个GUID（不是应用来源代码）：\n+\n+- shared/fwptypes.h与fwpmtypes.h核对BLOCK的终止动作位、EQUAL=0、DYNAMIC=1；没有取第三方P/Invoke实现或本应用同功能代码。\n+\n+### 7.3 HDC边界、人工条件和不能承诺的部分\n+\n+- **HDC保护依据**：只在AUTH_CONNECT层按Emulator block前创建DYNAMIC会话并原子加入V4/V6，随后GetById核对返回对象，再回ACK_BLOCKED；任一步失败Abort/Close，回ERROR_UNBLOCKED。ACK只证明helper已配置对象，不证明NAT已断。\n+- Close恢复依赖本地helper进程，不依赖HDC；正常unblock/退出和异常进程终止都释放动态会话。记录session GUID/filter The original installed Emulator paths are never accepted as targets.\\r\\n- Exactly one readable process at that path, the specified PID and exact UTC StartTime, expected binary SHA256, command line `-instance VgSpec1ManualOffline`, explicit `-hvdport 11237`, and `-path` equal to the specified instance root are required.\\r\\n- Instance root and run/control directory must be existing children of `D:\\\\HCUP\\\\vg-spec1\\\\logs\\\\`. Reparse points/junctions in those paths are rejected. No control message can change any target parameter.\\r\\n- WFP matches the executable **APP_ID/path**, not PID. PID/StartTime/instance checks are user-mode guards. Another process at the same copied path would temporarily share the path condition until the next guard check; starting it during the experiment is prohibited. Detection closes the session and exits with an error. The original executable\'s other instances do not share this copied path.\\r\\n- Only two outbound layers are used: ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V4 and V6. Each filter has exactly one EQUAL/BYTE_BLOB ALE_APP_ID condition and BLOCK action, flags zero, and a new owned nonpersistent sublayer. No loopback exception, endpoint/port limitation, RECEIVE/LISTEN filter, kernel driver, Windows Firewall setting, BFE/ACL change or global audit collection is used.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Build and read-only check (ordinary terminal)\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\n& \'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/Build-Guard.ps1\'\\r\\n& \'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/bin/VgSpec1WfpGuard.exe\' --check\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe build script loads the required Harmony environment, invokes the installed x64 .NET Framework compiler with warnings as errors, and runs only `--check`. It writes each attempt\'s compiler/check output under `logs/development-round-03/wfp-build/` and a source/binary SHA256 manifest under `bin/`. No downloads, NuGet packages or new compiler are needed. Rebuilding changes the executable hash; use the final reviewed manifest.\\r\\n\\r\\nNo arguments also means check. This mode only reads ABI sizes/offsets, administrator-token status, fixed file presence/hash and, if all target options are supplied, process guards. It never calls EngineOpen or any WFP API. The `nativeWfpCalls:0` field records that code path; it is not a trace of an elevated experiment. If the copied tool does not exist, basic check still succeeds and reports its absence; live target validation remains unverified.\\r\\n\\r\\nAn optional check with `--target-pid`, `--target-start-utc`, `--target-sha256`, and `--instance-root` performs the same read-only target guard. Exact StartTime should come from `(Get-Process -Id <PID>).StartTime.ToUniversalTime().ToString(\'o\')`. No target is guessed or created by this helper.\\r\\n\\r\\n## User\'s manual elevated entry (do not run during preparation)\\r\\n\\r\\nThe root/verification role first copies the complete official installed emulator tool directory into the fixed isolated directory, then starts only the reviewed task instance using an explicit task-local `-path` and port. This helper does not copy or start it. A fresh run directory and 32 lowercase hexadecimal nonce must be prepared by the controller. Do not reuse a directory containing `status.json` or `helper.lock`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe **user** opens an administrator PowerShell console and runs the reviewed entry with actual PID/time/hash/root values:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\n& \'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/Start-GuardManually.ps1\' `\\r\\n  -TargetPid <ACTUAL_PID> -TargetStartUtc \'<EXACT_UTC_STARTTIME>\' `\\r\\n  -TargetSha256 \'<EXPECTED_64_LOWERCASE_HEX>\' `\\r\\n  -InstanceRoot \'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/logs/<reviewed-instance-root>\' `\\r\\n  -RunDirectory \'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/logs/<fresh-run-directory>\' `\\r\\n  -RunNonce \'<32_LOWERCASE_HEX>\' -MaxSeconds 1200 -MaxBlockSeconds 600\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThis script requires an already elevated console and checks the built EXE and source hashes. It never invokes UAC/RunAs. Do not substitute paths or omit independent review. `--serve` refuses unelevated callers before any WFP call. It starts **IDLE_UNBLOCKED**, with no engine open and no filters. Only an accepted block request opens the dynamic engine and adds objects.\\r\\n\\r\\nTotal runtime defaults to 1200 seconds, hard range 30–1800. Each continuous block defaults to 600 seconds, hard range 5–900, and can never extend past the total deadline. A successful repeated block is idempotent and cannot extend its absolute block deadline. Monotonic time enforces these limits. The watchdog checks target/lease/deadlines once per second; target binary size/mtime is checked each tick and full SHA256 is forced every ten seconds and immediately before blocking. A changed/unreadable target, second same-path process, stale controller or deadline causes cleanup, an explicit error status and exit. Startup allows at most 45 seconds for the first fresh request.\\r\\n\\r\\nAn independent background watchdog checks the same monotonic total/lease/block deadlines every 250 ms. If a synchronous BFE/WMI call prevents the normal close/error path for more than three seconds past a deadline, it terminates the management process with FailFast so Windows dynamic-session/RPC cleanup can run. That abnormal exit and any stale status must fail the facility gate; it cannot be treated as a normal acknowledgment. No global audit policy is changed. Actual crash/rundown recovery is still an elevated validation item.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Control protocol (ordinary controller, no privileges)\\r\\n\\r\\nThe only input is `<RunDirectory>/request.json`, strict UTF-8 JSON, at most 4096 bytes, with exactly these five fields:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\"nonce\\":\\"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\\",\\"sequence\\":1,\\"operation\\":\\"unblock\\",\\"createdUtc\\":\\"2026-10-17T10:00:00.0000000Z\\",\\"expiresUtc\\":\\"2026-10-17T10:00:10.0000000Z\\"}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the actual nonce and current UTC times. Allowed operations are exactly `block`, `unblock`, `exit`. Sequence is a strictly increasing positive integer. Creation can be at most two seconds in the future or fifteen seconds old; expiration must be later than creation/current time and at most fifteen seconds after creation. Wrong nonce/sequence/fields/operation/expired messages are rejected and do not renew the lease. The old unchanged file never renews it. Emit a new atomic replacement every three seconds with a ten-second lease while the test is active, including while unblocked. On lost lease the helper closes and exits **ERROR_UNBLOCKED**, code 3; that must fail the facility gate, never silently become a passing cancellation case. A new nonce cannot be adopted by the existing helper.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor individual requests, the supplied ordinary-user writer performs atomic replacement:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\n& \'D:/HCUP/vg-spec1/hypium_tests/network_isolation/Send-GuardRequest.ps1\' `\\r\\n  -RunDirectory \'<SAME_RUN_DIRECTORY>\' -RunNonce \'<SAME_NONCE>\' `\\r\\n  -Sequence 1 -Operation unblock -LeaseSeconds 10\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe controller\'s next request uses sequence 2, and so forth. A writer\'s output is not a helper acknowledgment. Wait for matching nonce/accepted sequence and the required state in `status.json`; keep auditing that heartbeat and the unchanged deadline/filter IDs.\\r\\n\\r\\n`status.json` is replaced atomically once per tick and after termination:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `schemaVersion`, `task`, `nonce`, `state`, `active` (boolean), `helperPid`, `timestampUtc`.\\r\\n- `lastAcceptedSequence`, nullable `lastAcceptedUtc`, `requestExpiresUtc`, `totalDeadlineUtc`, nullable `blockDeadlineUtc`.\\r\\n- `target`: fixed `path`, `pid`, exact `startTimeUtc`, `sha256`, fixed `instance`, `instanceRoot`, `hdcPort` (string `11237`), `guardOk` and `lastGuardUtc` (last successful guard).\\r\\n- `filters`: empty before/after block; while BLOCKED exactly two objects with `id` (decimal string), `key`, `layerGuid`, `layerName`, `verified:true`.\\r\\n- `nativeEngineOpen`, `sessionGuid`, `subLayerGuid`, nullable `terminationReason`, `auditMode:not_enabled`, `proof:filter_configuration_only`.\\r\\n\\r\\nState literals are `IDLE_UNBLOCKED`, `BLOCKED`, `EXITED_UNBLOCKED`, `ERROR_UNBLOCKED`, and exceptional `ERROR_CLEANUP_UNCONFIRMED`. The last state means NativeClose failed: never claim recovery from that snapshot; the process exits with code 4 so Windows RPC rundown can clean its dynamic objects, followed by independent recovery verification. The normal error exit code is 3. `terminationReason` is null while running and records exit_request/console_cancel or the specific failed guard/deadline/lease/API cause at termination.\\r\\n\\r\\n`helper.jsonl` records ready, armed, control accepted/rejected, each DWORD-returning native call result, filter ID/layer/key, exact target path/hash, APP_ID blob hash, session/sublayer GUID and cleanup. Pre-commit and post-commit GetById verify identity, owned sublayer, flags, exact single APP_ID condition/type/match/blob and BLOCK action. If same-transaction GetById cannot read newly added filters, the transaction is aborted and the engine closed: there is no fallback that skips this verification. That visibility and all API behavior remain untested until an approved elevated run. No WFP net-event/drop audit has been enabled or claimed.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Recovery\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Send a current nonce/sequence `unblock`, then check matching `IDLE_UNBLOCKED`, active false, engine false, empty filters, and the real NAT recovery control.\\r\\n2. Send current `exit`, or press Ctrl+C in the manually opened helper console. Both close the dynamic session and terminate.\\r\\n3. If the controller/HDC is unavailable, use the helper console\'s Ctrl+C. As a last local recovery, the user may terminate only the recorded helper PID after checking its executable path/StartTime. Terminating this management process ends the dynamic WFP session; do not kill unrelated Emulator or HDC processes.\\r\\n4. Unexpected process death also ends the dynamic session by the official WFP lifecycle contract. A stale status file is not a live acknowledgment; independently confirm restored same-endpoint HEAD/GET. There are no persistent/boot-time rules to restore, no global defaults were changed, and no broad cleanup rule should be run.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe independent sequence remains online positive control → scoped block plus same-endpoint failure/zero arrivals and host-service liveness → three cancellation cases with full evidence → unblock/exit and same-endpoint recovery. Check HDC heartbeat and lawful reconnection throughout. A guest may still report eth0/NetConn available: this helper targets transmission isolation, not the guest network-manager state. Do not report R27 passed until the root agent reviews the independent evidence and this boundary.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Primary references\\r\\n\\r\\nNative types/constants/GUIDs are based on Microsoft\'s [WinSDK fwpmtypes.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/shared/fwpmtypes.h), [fwptypes.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/shared/fwptypes.h), [fwpmu.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/um/fwpmu.h) and [rpcdce.h](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata/blob/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/shared/rpcdce.h). You can try changing directories.\\nL24: # Filter Arbitration\\nL25: \\nL26: Feedback\\nL27: \\nL28: Summarize this article for me\\nL29: \\nL30: ## In this article\\nL31: \\nL32: Filter arbitration is the logic built into the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) that is used to determine how filters interact with each other when making network traffic filtering decisions.\\nL33: ## Filter Arbitration Behaviors\\nL34: \\nL35: The following behaviors characterize the filter arbitration system:\\nL36:   * All traffic can be inspected. No traffic can bypass filters at a given layer.\\nL37:   * Traffic can be blocked by a callout filter via a Veto even if a higher priority filter has permitted it.\\nL38:   * Multiple providers can inspect traffic at the same layer. For example, firewall followed by intrusion-detection system (IDS) filters, or IPsec followed by Quality of Service (QoS) filters may all examine the traffic at the same layer.\\nL39: ## Filtering Model\\nL40: \\nL41: Each filter layer is divided into sub-layers ordered by priority (also called weight). Network traffic traverses sub-layers from the highest priority to the lowest priority. Sub-layers are created and managed by the developers using the WFP API.\\nL42: \\nL43: Within each sub-layer, filters are ordered by weight. Network traffic is indicated to matching filters from highest weight to lowest weight.\\nL44: The filter arbitration algorithm is applied to all sub-layers within a layer and the final filtering decision is made after all sub-layers have been evaluated. This provides for multiple matching capability.\\nL45: \\nL46: Within a sub-layer, filter arbitration is performed as follows:\\nL47:   * Compute the list of matching filters ordered by weight from highest to lowest.\\nL48:   * Evaluate matching filters in order until a \\"Permit\\" or a \\"Block\\" is returned (filters can also return \\"Continue\\") or until the list is exhausted.\\nL49:   * Skip the remaining filters and return the action from the last evaluated filter.\\nL50: \\nL51: Within a layer, filter arbitration is performed as follows:\\nL52:   * Perform filter arbitration at every sub-layer in order from highest priority to lowest priority.\\nL53:   * Evaluate all sub-layers even if a higher priority sub-layer has decided to block the traffic.\\nL54:   * Return the resulting action based on the policy rules described in the following section.\\nL55: The diagram below illustrates a sample sub-layer configuration. The outer boxes represent layers. The inner boxes represent sub-layers that contain filters. The wildcard (*) in a filter means all traffic matches the filter.\\nL56: \\nL57: \ue200cite\ue2025†Image: sample sub-layer configuration\ue201 L58: The only way for a filter to be bypassed is if a higher weight filter has permitted or blocked the traffic within the same sub-layer. Conversely, one way of ensuring that a filter always sees all traffic within a layer is to add a sub-layer that contains a single filter that matches all traffic.\\nL59: ## Configurable Override Policy\\nL60: \\nL61: The rules described below govern the arbitration decisions within a layer. These rules are used by the filter engine to decide which one of the sub-layer actions is applied to the network traffic.\\nL62: \\nL63: The basic policy is as follows.\\nL64: \\nL65:   * Actions are evaluated in priority order of sub-layers from highest priority to lowest priority.\\nL66:   * \\"Block\\" overrides \\"Permit\\".\\nL67:   * \\"Block\\" is final (cannot be overridden) and stops the evaluation. The packet is discarded.\\nL68: The basic policy does not support the scenario of an exception not overridden by a firewall. Typical examples of this type of scenario are:\\nL69: \\nL70:   * Remote administration port required to be opened even in the presence of a third-party firewall.\\nL71:   * Components that require ports to be opened in order to function (for example, Universal Plug and Play UPnP). If the administrator has explicitly enabled the component, the firewall should not silently block the traffic.\\nL72: In order to support the above scenarios, a filtering decision must be made more difficult to override than another filtering decision by managing the action override permission. This permission is implemented as the FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE flag and it is set on a per-filter basis.\\nL73: The evaluation algorithm maintains the current action (\\"Permit\\" or \\"Block\\") along with the FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE flag. The flag controls whether a lower priority sub-layer is allowed to override the action. By setting or resetting the FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE flag in the \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPS_CLASSIFY_OUT0\ue201 structure, a provider governs how actions can or cannot be overridden. If the flag is set, it indicates that the action can be overridden. If the flag is absent, the action cannot be overridden.\\nL74: Action  | Allow override (FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE is set)  | Description\\nL75: --- | --- | ---\\nL76: Permit  | Yes  | The traffic can be blocked at another sub-layer. This is called a soft permit.\\nL77: Permit  | No  | The traffic can be blocked at another sub-layer only by a callout Veto. This is called a hard permit.\\nL78: Block  | Yes  | The traffic can be permitted at another sub-layer. This is called a soft block.\\nL79: Block  | No  | The traffic cannot be permitted at another sub-layer. This is called a hard block.\\nL80: The filter action can be set by setting the type member in the structure \ue200cite\ue2027†FWPM_ACTION0\ue201 to either FWP_ACTION_BLOCK or FWP_ACTION_PERMIT. Along with the action type, a filter also exposes the flag FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHT. If this flag is cleared, then the action type is hard and cannot be overridden except when a hard permit is overridden by a Veto as explained later on, else it is soft which can be overridden by high priority action.\\nL81: The following table lists the default behavior for filter and callout actions.\\nL82: \\nL83: Action  | Default Behavior\\nL84: --- | ---\\nL85: Filter permit  | Soft permit\\nL86: Callout permit  | Soft permit\\nL87: Filter block  | Hard block\\nL88: Callout block  | Soft block\\nL89: \\nL90: A Veto is a \\"Block\\" action returned by the filter when the FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE flag was reset prior to calling the filter. A Veto will block traffic that was permitted with a hard permit.\\nL91: When a Veto is issued, it is an indication of conflict in the configuration. The following actions are taken to mitigate the conflict.\\nL92: \\nL93:   * The traffic is blocked.\\nL94: \\nL95:   * An audit event is generated.\\nL96: \\nL97:   * A notification is generated.\\nL98: \\nL99: Note\\nL100: \\nL101: The notification is received by all entities that have subscribed to it. This will typically include the firewall (in order to detect mis-configurations), or applications (in order to detect if their particular filter is overridden).\\nL102: \\nL103: Note\\nL104: There is no mandatory user interface (UI) instantiated when a \\"Hard Permit\\" filter is overridden. The notifications of the override are sent to any provider that registered to receive them, which allows firewalls, or the applications that created the \\"Permit\\" filters, to show UI asking for user action.\\nL105: There is no value in having a platform UI notification for these override events since firewall ISVs that do not want to silently block can do so by registering at a different place in WFP, or (less preferred) handle all their logic in a call-out driver. ISVs that do think prompting users is a good idea will want to own the user experience and create their own UI.\\nL106: The mitigation behavior described above ensures that a \\"Hard Permit\\" filter is not silently overridden by a \\"Block\\" filter, and covers the scenario where a remote administration port is not allowed to be blocked by the firewall. In order to silently override \\"Hard Permit\\" filters a firewall has to add its filters within a higher priority sub-layer.\\nL107: \\nL108: Note\\nL109: Since there is no cross-layer arbitration, traffic permitted with \\"Hard Permit\\" may still be blocked at another layer. It is the responsibility of the policy author to ensure that traffic is permitted at each layer if necessary.\\nL110: \\nL111: User applications requesting ports to be opened add overridable filters to a low priority sub-layer. The firewall can subscribe to the filter add notification events and add a matching filter after user (or policy) validation.\\nL112: ## Related topics\\nL113: \\nL114: \ue200cite\ue2028†Filter Weight BOM。它们未形成扩大过滤范围或续租绕过的已证路径，当前可信本地控制器按writer原样发送，不据此扩重构。若以后对协议形式作强安全承诺，应单独收紧并重封。\n+\n+## 4. 子层0x100的技术判断\n+\n+04 `WfpSession.cs:58`选择子层weight0x100；filter自身weight=EMPTY、默认BLOCK且flags=0。**不能仅因0x100较低便断言不会拦截，也不能据此保证会拦截。**[微软Filter Arbitration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/filter-arbitration)说明子层依优先级评估，普通Permit可被其他子层Block覆盖，默认filter block为hard；但更高优先级的hard permit会限制低优先级过滤器覆盖，callout veto另有规则。\n+\n+本辅助不是veto callout、未读取系统现有每条更高优先策略，故现时静态证据不足以证明loopback实际会被该权重阻断。它有独立随机子层、其中只有本题两个不同layer的filter，不存在自己子层内另一条高权过滤把它跳过的问题。不要为了预测结果盲目把权重改满或添加驱动；必须以同一10.0.2.2 NAT路径真实负对照、host活服务和HDC控制实测决定。\n+\n+## 5. Close后“无残留”的证据要求与05批准范围\n+\n+04只有主EngineClose0返回值与动态会话官方生命周期，实际恢复流量能证明可达；二者**不能独立排除原Block未生效而过滤对象仍残留**。root已批准05补最小fresh observer，未批准独立inspect模式或任意过滤器输入。\n+\n+要求顺序：保留本次真实两filterId和ownedSubLayerKey→主Close0成功→新只读engine→可选只读事务→GetById两个真实ID严格返回 `FWP_E_FILTER_NOT_FOUND=0x80320003`→SubLayerGetByKey本次GUID严格返回 `FWP_E_SUBLAYER_NOT_FOUND=0x80320007`→结束只读事务并close observer。不Add对象、不改policy、不启global audit。对象仍存在、AccessDenied、泛NOT_FOUND或其他错误，均不能当精确对象已不存在。\n+\n+observer中的Get/log/Abort异常也必须进入finally Close；主Close失败不启动查询来掩盖；observer失败后保留cleanup_unconfirmed，不允许后续无条件Close()覆盖成成功。闲置、从未添加对象的Close不用打开BFE；默认/--check仍须零WFP调用。独立watchdog覆盖新同步API挂起。\n+\n+主Agent选择的异常清理验证为：实际停止控制器心跳→lease错误→主Close及observer→ERROR_UNBLOCKED退出，随后真实同endpoint恢复正控；不需要杀helper再增加第二个人工管理员会话。这验证受控错误退出，不能表述为已测试进程崩溃/FailFast/rundown。\n+\n+一手依据：[FilterGetById0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfiltergetbyid0)、[SubLayerGetByKey0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmsublayergetbykey0)、[WFP Error Codes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/wfp-error-codes)。后两接口返回对象均须FwpmFreeMemory释放。错误码已独立查证，API权限/对象查询行为仍需真实管理员会话运行。\n+\n+## 6. 尚待05冻结复核及实际设施验收\n+\n+05待复核：精确官方CLI及拒绝案例、fresh observer全部资源路径/状态覆盖、默认--check零WFP、修订源码/EXEhash和实际identity只读检查。修订中不运行serve、不动设备生命周期。\n+\n+真实运行阶段必须分别证明：两filter实际回读正确且新鲜；NAT负控失败而host服务活着；HDC持续心跳/合法重连/UI；离线第一层等待/三取消与D0/UI0；主动unblock及lease错误清理后对象精确不存在、同NAT恢复正控。guest eth0/NetConn可能仍宣告可用，需按既有口径明确传输隔离与系统LinkDown差异。任何ACK、编译成功或静态审查均不替代这些结果。\n*** End Patch"));

You can try changing directories.\\nL24: # FwpmFilterAdd0 function (fwpmu.h)\\nL25: \\nL26: Feedback\\nL27: \\nL28: Summarize this article for me\\nL29: \\nL30: ## In this article\\nL31: \\nL32: The FwpmFilterAdd0 function adds a new filter object to the system.\\nL33: \\nL34: ## Syntax\\nL35: \\nL36:     `DWORD FwpmFilterAdd0(\\nL37:       [in]            HANDLE               engineHandle,\\nL38:       [in]            const FWPM_FILTER0   *filter,\\nL39:       [in, optional]  PSECURITY_DESCRIPTOR sd,\\nL40:       [out, optional] UINT64               *id\\nL41:     );\\nL42:     `\\nL43: ## Parameters\\nL44: \\nL45: `[in] engineHandle`\\nL46: \\nL47: Type: HANDLE\\nL48: \\nL49: Handle for an open session to the filter engine. Call \ue200cite\ue2025†FwpmEngineOpen0\ue201 to open a session to the filter engine.\\nL50: \\nL51: `[in] filter`\\nL52: \\nL53: Type: \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPM_FILTER0\ue201 *\\nL54: \\nL55: The filter object to be added.\\nL56: \\nL57: `[in, optional] sd`\\nL58: \\nL59: Type: \ue200cite\ue2027†SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR\ue201 L60: \\nL61: Security information about the filter object.\\nL62: \\nL63: `[out, optional] id`\\nL64: \\nL65: Type: UINT64*\\nL66: \\nL67: The runtime identifier for this filter.\\nL68: ## Return value\\nL69: \\nL70: Type: DWORD\\nL71: Return code/value  | Description\\nL72: --- | ---\\nL73: ERROR_SUCCESS\\nL74: 0  | The filter was successfully added.\\nL75: ERROR_INVALID_SECURITY_DESCR\\nL76: 0x8007053A  | The security descriptor structure is invalid. Or, a filter condition contains a security descriptor in absolute format.\\nL77: FWP_E_CALLOUT_NOTIFICATION_FAILED\\nL78: 0x80320037  | The caller added a callout filter and the callout returned an error from its notification routine.\\nL79: FWP_E_* error code\\nL80: 0x80320001—0x80320039  | A Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) specific error. See \ue200cite\ue2028†WFP Error Codes\ue201 for details.\\nL81: RPC_* error code\\nL82: 0x80010001—0x80010122  | Failure to communicate with the remote or local firewall engine.\\nL83: ## Remarks\\nL84: \\nL85: FwpmFilterAdd0 adds the filter to the specified sub-layer at every filtering layer in the system.\\nL86: \\nL87: Some fields in the \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPM_FILTER0\ue201 structure are assigned by the system, not the caller, and are ignored in the call to FwpmFilterAdd0.\\nL88: \\nL89: If the caller supplies a NULL security descriptor, the system will assign a default security descriptor.\\nL90: To block connections to particular locations, add a \ue200cite\ue2029†FWP_ACTION_BLOCK\ue201 filter specifying the local address at the \ue200cite\ue20210†FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V*\ue201 layer, or add a FWP_ACTION_BLOCK filter without specifying the local address at the FWPM_LAYER_ALE_RESOURCE_ASSIGNMENT_V* layer.\\nL91: \\nL92: Note\\nL93: \\nL94: If a local address is specified at the resource assignment layer, an implicit bind would succeed because address, address type, and port may come back as \ue200cite\ue20211†FWP_EMPTY\ue201 .\\nL95: The \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPM_FILTER0\ue201 structure can label a filter as a boot-time or persistent filter. Boot-time filters are added to the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) when the TCP/IP driver starts, and are removed once the BFE finishes initialization. Persistent objects are added when the BFE starts.\\nL96: \\nL97: This function cannot be called from within a read-only transaction. It will fail with FWP_E_INCOMPATIBLE_TXN. See \ue200cite\ue20212†Object Management\ue201 for more information about transactions.\\nL98: \\nL99: The caller needs the following access rights:\\nL100:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD\ue201 access to the filter\'s container\\nL101:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\ue201 access to the provider (if any)\\nL102:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\ue201 access to the applicable layer\\nL103:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\ue201 access to the applicable sub-layer\\nL104:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\ue201 access to the callout (if any)\\nL105:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\ue201 access to the provider context (if any).\\nL106: \\nL107: See \ue200cite\ue20214†Access Control\ue201 for more information.\\nL108: \\nL109: To add a filter that references a callout, invoke the functions in the following order.\\nL110:   * Call \ue200cite\ue20215†FwpsCalloutRegister0\ue201 (documented in the Windows Driver Kit (WDK)), to register the callout with the filter engine.\\nL111:   * Call \ue200cite\ue20216†FwpmCalloutAdd0\ue201 to add the callout to the system.\\nL112:   * Call FwpmFilterAdd0 to add the filter that references the callout to the system.\\nL113: \\nL114: By default filters that reference callouts that have been added but have not yet registered with the filter engine are treated as Block filters.\\nL115: FwpmFilterAdd0 is a specific implementation of FwpmFilterAdd. See \ue200cite\ue20217†WFP Version-Independent Names and Targeting Specific Versions of Windows\ue201 for more information.\\nL116: #### Examples\\nL117: The following C++ example shows how to initialize and add a filter using FwpmFilterAdd0 that\\nL118: specifically blocks traffic on IP V4 for all applications.\\nL119: \\nL120:     `\\nL121:     // Add filter to block traffic on IP V4 for all applications.\\nL122:     //\\nL123:     FWPM_FILTER0      fwpFilter;\\nL124:     FWPM_SUBLAYER0    fwpFilterSubLayer;\\nL125: \\nL126:     RtlZeroMemory(&fwpFilter, sizeof(FWPM_FILTER0));\\nL127: \\nL128:     fwpFilter.layerKey = FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V4;\\nL129:     fwpFilter.action.type = FWP_ACTION_BLOCK;\\nL130:     if (&fwpFilterSubLayer.subLayerKey != NULL)\\nL131:         fwpFilter.subLayerKey = fwpFilterSubLayer.subLayerKey;\\nL132: \\nL133:     fwpFilter.weight.type = FWP_EMPTY; // auto-weight.\\nL134:     fwpFilter.numFilterConditions = 0; // this applies to all application traffic\\nL135:     fwpFilter.displayData.name = L\\"Receive/Accept Layer Block\\";\\nL136:     fwpFilter.displayData.description = L\\"Filter to block all inbound connections.\\";\\nL137: \\nL138:     printf(\\"Adding filter to block all inbound connections.\\\\n\\");\\nL139:     result = FwpmFilterAdd0(engineHandle, &fwpFilter, NULL, NULL);\\nL140: \\nL141:     if (result != ERROR_SUCCESS)\\nL142:         printf(\\"FwpmFilterAdd0 failed. A Veto is a "Block" action returned by the filter when the FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE flag was reset prior to calling the filter.\n  * Evaluate all sub-layers even if a higher priority sub-layer has decided to block the traffic.\n  * Return the resulting action based on the policy rules described in the following section.\n\nThe diagram below illustrates a sample sub-layer configuration. The outer boxes represent layers. The inner boxes represent sub-layers that contain filters. The wildcard (*) in a filter means all traffic matches the filter.\n\nImage: sample sub-layer configuration\n\nThe only way for a filter to be bypassed is if a higher weight filter has permitted or blocked the traffic within the same sub-layer. Conversely, one way of ensuring that a filter always sees all traffic within a layer is to add a sub-layer that contains a single filter that matches all traffic.\n\n## Configurable Override Policy\n\nThe rules described below govern the arbitration decisions within a layer. These rules are used by the filter engine to decide which one of the sub-layer actions is applied to the network traffic.\n\nThe basic policy is as follows.\n\n  * Actions are evaluated in priority order of sub-layers from highest priority to lowest priority.\n  * "Block" overrides "Permit".\n  * "Block" is final (cannot be overridden) and stops the evaluation. The packet is discarded.\n\nThe basic policy does not support the scenario of an exception not overridden by a firewall. Typical examples of this type of scenario are:\n\n  * Remote administration port required to be opened even in the presence of a third-party firewall.\n  * Components that require ports to be opened in order to function (for example, Universal Plug and Play UPnP). If the administrator has explicitly enabled the component, the firewall should not silently block the traffic.\n\nIn order to support the above scenarios, a filtering decision must be made more difficult to override than another filtering decision by managing the action override permission. This permission is implemented as the FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE flag and it is set on a per-filter basis.\n\nThe evaluation algorithm maintains the current action ("Permit" or "Block") along with the FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE flag. The flag controls whether a lower priority sub-layer is allowed to override the action. By setting or resetting the FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE flag in the FWPS_CLASSIFY_OUT0 structure, a provider governs how actions can or cannot be overridden. If the flag is set, it indicates that the action can be overridden. If the flag is absent, the action cannot be overridden.\n\nExpand table\n\nAction  | Allow override (FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE is set)  | Description\n--- | --- | ---\nPermit  | Yes  | The traffic can be blocked at another sub-layer. This is called a soft permit.\nPermit  | No  | The traffic can be blocked at another sub-layer only by a callout Veto. This is called a hard permit.\nBlock  | Yes  | The traffic can be permitted at another sub-layer. This is called a soft block.\nBlock  | No  | The traffic cannot be permitted at another sub-layer. This is called a hard block.\n\nThe filter action can be set by setting the type member in the structure FWPM_ACTION0 to either FWP_ACTION_BLOCK or FWP_ACTION_PERMIT. Along with the action type, a filter also exposes the flag FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHT. If this flag is cleared, then the action type is hard and cannot be overridden except when a hard permit is overridden by a Veto as explained later on, else it is soft which can be overridden by high priority action.\n\nThe following table lists the default behavior for filter and callout actions.\n\nExpand table\n\nAction  | Default Behavior\n--- | ---\nFilter permit  | Soft permit\nCallout permit  | Soft permit\nFilter block  | Hard block\nCallout block  | Soft block\n\nA Veto is a "Block" action returned by the filter when the FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE flag was reset prior to calling the filter. A Veto will block traffic that was permitted with a hard permit.\n\nWhen a Veto is issued, it is an indication of conflict in the configuration. The following actions are taken to mitigate the conflict.\n\n  * The traffic is blocked.\n\n  * An audit event is generated.\n\n  * A notification is generated.\n\nNote\n\nThe notification is received by all entities that have subscribed to it. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nFWPM_FILTER0 (fwpmtypes.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmtypes/ns-fwpmtypes-fwpm_filter0)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn39search1\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last month; **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHT** ...  | BFE will automatically assign a weight based on the filter conditions.\n\n## Members\n\n`filterKey`\n\nUniquely identifies the session.\n\nIf the GUID is initialized to zero in the call to FwpmFilterAdd0, the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) will generate one.\n\n`displayData`\n\nA FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 structure that contains human-readable annotations associated with the filter. The name member of the FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 structure is required.\n\n`flags`\n\nA combination of the following values.\n\nExpand table\n\nFilter flag  | Meaning\n--- | ---\n\n**FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_NONE**\n | Default.\n\n**FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_PERSISTENT**\n | Filter is persistent, that is, it survives across BFE stop/start. **Note**\xa0\xa0This flag cannot be set together with **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_BOOTTIME**. \xa0\n\n**FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_BOOTTIME**\n | Filter is enforced at boot-time, even before BFE starts. **Note**\xa0\xa0This flag cannot be set together with **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_PERSISTENT**. \xa0\n\n**FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_HAS_PROVIDER_CONTEXT**\n | Filter references a provider context.\n\n**FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHT**\n | Clear filter action right.\n\n**FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_PERMIT_IF_CALLOUT_UNREGISTERED**\n | If the callout is not registered, the filter is treated as a permit filter. **Note**\xa0\xa0This flag can be set only if the **action** type is **FWP_ACTION_CALLOUT_TERMINATING** or **FWP_ACTION_CALLOUT_UNKNOWN**. \xa0\n\n**FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_DISABLED**\n | Filter is disabled. A provider\'s filters are disabled when the BFE starts if the provider has no associated Windows service name, or if the associated service is not set to auto-start. **Note**\xa0\xa0This flag cannot be set when adding new filters. It can only be returned by BFE when getting or enumerating filters. \xa0\n\n**FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_INDEXED**\n | Filter is indexed to help enable faster lookup during classification. **Note**\xa0\xa0Available only in Windows\xa08 and Windows Server\xa02012. \xa0\n\n`providerKey`\n\nOptional GUID of the policy provider that manages this filter. See Built-in Provider Identifiers for a list of predefined policy providers.\n\n`providerData`\n\nA FWP_BYTE_BLOB structure that contains optional provider-specific data used by providers to store additional context information with the object.\n\n`layerKey`\n\nGUID of the layer where the filter resides. See Filtering Layer Identifiers for a list of possible values.\n\n`subLayerKey`\n\nGUID of the sub-layer where the filter resides. See Filtering Sub-Layer Identifiers for a list of built-in sub-layers.\n\nIf this is set to IID_NULL, the filter is added to the default sublayer.\n\n`weight`\n\nA FWP_VALUE0 structure that specifies the weight of the filter. The weight indicates the priority of the filter, where higher-numbered weights have higher priorities (and will be evaluated before lower-weighted filters).\n\nPossible type values for weight are as follows.\n\nExpand table\n\n**weight** type  | Meaning\n--- | ---\n\n**FWP_UINT64**\n | BFE will use the supplied value as the filter\'s weight.\n\n**FWP_UINT8**\n0–15\n | BFE will use the supplied value as a weight range index and will compute the filter\'s weight in that range. See Filter Weight Assignment for more information.\n\n**FWP_EMPTY**\n | BFE will automatically assign a weight based on the filter conditions.\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nFWPM_FILTER0 (fwpmtypes.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/ru-ru/windows/win32/api/fwpmtypes/ns-fwpmtypes-fwpm_filter0)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn39search2\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last week; **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHT**\n      GUID                   *reserved;\n      UINT64                 filterId;\n      FWP_VALUE0             effectiveWeight;\n    } FWPM_FILTER0;\n\n## Члены\n\n`filterKey`\n\nУникально идентифицирует сеанс.\n\nЕсли guid инициализирован равным нулю в вызове FwpmFilterAdd0, модуль базовой фильтрации (BFE) создаст его.\n\n`displayData`\n\nСтруктура FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 , содержащая доступные для чтения заметки, связанные с фильтром. Filters in kernel-mode layers can be marked as boot-time filters by passing the appropriate flag to FwpmFilterAdd0.\n\n# Object Management\n\nFeedback\n\nSummarize this article for me\n\n## In this article\n\n  1. Sessions\n  2. Transactions\n  3. Object Lifetimes\n  4. Object Associations\n  5. LUIDs and GUIDs\n\nThis section covers the correct use of Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) API object types.\n\n## Sessions\n\nThe WFP API is session-oriented, and most function calls are made within the context of a session. A new client session is created by calling FwpmEngineOpen0. The session ends either when the client calls FwpmEngineClose0 or the client process terminates. When a session is destroyed, either on purpose or by the RPC rundown, the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) first aborts any existing transaction.\n\nWhen creating a new session, the caller can create a dynamic session by passing the FWPM_SESSION_FLAG_DYNAMIC flag to FwpmEngineOpen0. Any objects added during a dynamic session are automatically deleted when the session ends.\n\n## Transactions\n\nThe WFP API is transactional, and most function calls are made within the context of a transaction. \n  * Aborting the transaction, in which case none of the filters will be added.\n  * Committing the transaction, in which case the first three filters will be added.\n  * Continuing with more operations including potentially retrying the failed FwpmFilterAdd0.\n\nWhen beginning a transaction, BFE will wait until the session\'s txnWaitTimeoutInMSec expires to acquire the lock. If the lock is not acquired within this time, the lock acquisition (and the FwpmTransactionBegin0 call) will fail. This prevents clients from indefinitely failing to respond. If the client did not specify a lock timeout, it defaults to 15 seconds.\n\nEach transaction also has a lock timeout. This is the maximum amount of time that it can own the lock. If the owner does not release the lock within this time, the transaction is forcibly aborted, causing the lock to be released. The lock timeout is not configurable. It is infinite for kernel-mode callers and one hour for user-mode callers. If a transaction is forcibly aborted, the next call made within that transaction will fail with FWP_E_TXN_ABORTED.\n\n## Object Lifetimes\n\nObjects can have one of four possible lifetimes:\n\n  * Dynamic — An object is dynamic only if it is added using a dynamic session handle. Dynamic objects live until they are deleted or the owning session terminates.\n  * Static — Objects are static by default. Static objects live until they are deleted, BFE stops, or the system is shutdown.\n  * Persistent — Persistent objects are created by passing the appropriate FWPM_*_FLAG_PERSISTENT flag to an Fwpm*Add0 function. Persistent objects live until they are deleted.\n  * Built-in — Built-in objects are predefined by BFE and cannot be added or deleted. They live forever.\n\nFilters in kernel-mode layers can be marked as boot-time filters by passing the appropriate flag to FwpmFilterAdd0. Boot-time filters are added to the system when the TCP/IP driver starts, and removed when BFE finishes initialization. Persistent objects are added when BFE starts.\n\nIn many cases, a policy provider may not want its persistent policy enforced if the provider has been disabled. When adding a provider, the caller can specify an optional Windows service name. When adding persistent objects, the caller can optionally specify the provider that "owns" that object. At service start, BFE only adds persistent objects to the system if they are not associated with a provider, or the associated provider has no Windows service name, or the associated Windows service is set to auto-start.\n\n## Object Associations\n\nSome objects have references to other objects. For example, a filter always references a layer and may reference a callout and a provider context. Objects cannot refer to objects that may have a shorter lifetime. Thus, a dynamic object cannot refer to a dynamic object from a different session. A static object cannot refer to a dynamic object. A persistent object cannot refer to a dynamic object, a static object, or a persistent object owned by a different provider.\n\nAn object cannot be deleted until all objects that reference it have first been deleted.\n\n## LUIDs and GUIDs\n\nAll user mode WFP API objects (FWPM) are identified by a globally unique identifier (GUID) and reference other objects by their GUIDs. The GUID need only be unique within the object type. For example, a filter and a provider context can have the same GUID, but two filters cannot. When adding a new object, callers can assign the object\'s GUID or leave it zero-initialized and let BFE assign the GUID.\n\nAll kernel mode WFP API objects (FWPS) are identified by a locally unique identifier (LUID) and reference other objects by their LUID. The switch from GUID to LUID enables WFP to conserve non-paged pool and optimize run-time processing. The width of the LUID depends on the object type and ranges from a UINT16 to a UINT64. LUIDs are always assigned by BFE.\n\n  * Last updated on 08/19/2020--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nフィルターアービトレーション - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/ja-jp/windows/win32/fwp/filter-arbitration)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn39search8\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Published: 1.6 years ago; Crawled: 2 months ago; 評価アルゴリズムでは、現在のアクション ("Permit" または "Block") が FWPS_RIGHT_ACTION_WRITE フラグと共に保持されます。 ... アクションの種類と共に、フィルターはフラグ FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHTも公開します。\nこれはソフト ブロックと呼ばれます。\nブロック  | いいえ  | 別のサブレイヤーでトラフィックを許可することはできません。 これはハード ブロックと呼ばれます。\n\nフィルター アクションは、構造体 FWPM_ACTION0 内の 型 メンバーを FWP_ACTION_BLOCK または FWP_ACTION_PERMITに設定することで設定できます。 アクションの種類と共に、フィルターはフラグ FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHTも公開します。 このフラグをクリアすると、後で説明するように、ハード許可が Veto によってオーバーライドされる場合を除き、アクションの種類はハードであり、オーバーライドできません。それ以外の場合は、優先度の高いアクションによってオーバーライドできるソフトです。\n\n次の表に、フィルターアクションと吹き出しアクションの既定の動作を示します。\n\nテーブルを展開する\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nArbitraggio filtro - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/it-it/windows/win32/fwp/filter-arbitration)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn39search9\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Published: 1.6 years ago; Crawled: 2 months ago; L\'azione di filtro può essere impostata impostando il tipo di membro nella struttura FWPM_ACTION0 su FWP_ACTION_BLOCK o FWP_ACTION_PERMIT.Insieme al tipo di azione, un filtro espone anche il flag FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHT.\nSi tratta di un permesso soft.\nPermettere  | No  | Il traffico può essere bloccato a un altro livello secondario solo da un callout Veto. Once the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) starts in user mode, persistent filters are added to the platform, boot-time filters are disabled, and notifications are sent to those callout drivers that subscribed using FwpmBfeStateSubscribeChanges0.\nUsers can also add their own sub-layers.\n\nThe list of filter engine layers is provided in the reference section topic Filtering Layer Identifiers.\n\n## Filters\n\nA filter is a rule that is matched against incoming or outgoing packets. The rule tells the filtering engine what to do with the packet, including to call a callout module for deep packet or stream inspection. For example, a filter may specify "Block traffic with a TCP port greater than 1024" or "Call out to IDS for all traffic that is not secured."\n\nA boot-time filter is a filter that is enforced at boot-time as soon as the TCP/IP stack driver (tcpip.sys) starts. A boot-time filter is disabled when BFE starts. A filter is marked as boot-time by setting the FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_BOOTTIME flag when FwpmFilterAdd0 is invoked.\n\nA run-time filter is a filter that is enforced after BFE starts. A run-time filter can be static, dynamic, or persistent depending on the way it was created. See Object Management for more information on the different types of run-time filters and their lifetime.\nFor one packet, stream, or event there is one classification call per layer.\n\nDuring classification, the properties (for example, source address) of the packet, stream, or event are compared with filter conditions set on filters at the layer where the classification is invoked. When matches are found, the Filter Arbitration algorithm is used to determines the result of the classification process.\n\nA classification request is triggered by a shim.\n\nClassification actions could be either:\n\n  * Permit\n  * Block\n  * Callout\n    * Permit\n    * Block\n    * Continue\n    * Defer\n    * Need more data\n    * Drop connection\n\n## WFP Operation\n\nAt boot-time, as soon as the TCP/IP stack driver (tcpip.sys) starts, the kernel-mode filter engine enforces the security policy of the system through boot-time filters.\n\nOnce the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) starts in user mode, persistent filters are added to the platform, boot-time filters are disabled, and notifications are sent to those callout drivers that subscribed using FwpmBfeStateSubscribeChanges0. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nFWPM_FILTER0 (fwpmtypes.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/es-es/windows/win32/api/fwpmtypes/ns-fwpmtypes-fwpm_filter0)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn39search11\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Published: 3.5 years ago; Crawled: last month; **FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_CLEAR_ACTION_RIGHT**\n      union {\n        UINT64 rawContext;\n        GUID   providerContextKey;\n      };\n      GUID                   *reserved;\n      UINT64                 filterId;\n      FWP_VALUE0             effectiveWeight;\n    } FWPM_FILTER0;\n    `\n\n## Miembros\n\n`filterKey`\n\nIdentifica de forma única la sesión.\n\nSi el GUID se inicializa en cero en la llamada a FwpmFilterAdd0, el motor de filtrado base (BFE) generará uno.\n\n`displayData`\n\nEstructura FWPM_DISPLAY_DATA0 que contiene anotaciones legibles para personas asociadas al filtro. `WfpSession.cs:58`选择子层weight0x100；filter自身weight=EMPTY、默认BLOCK且flags=0。**不能仅因0x100较低便断言不会拦截，也不能据此保证会拦截。**[微软Filter Arbitration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/filter-arbitration)说明子层依优先级评估，普通Permit可被其他子层Block覆盖，默认filter block为hard；但更高优先级的hard permit会限制低优先级过滤器覆盖，callout veto另有规则。\\r\\n\\r\\n本辅助不是veto callout、未读取系统现有每条更高优先策略，故现时静态证据不足以证明loopback实际会被该权重阻断。它有独立随机子层、其中只有本题两个不同layer的filter，不存在自己子层内另一条高权过滤把它跳过的问题。不要为了预测结果盲目把权重改满或添加驱动；必须以同一10.0.2.2 NAT路径真实负对照、host活服务和HDC控制实测决定。\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Close后“无残留”的证据要求与05批准范围\\r\\n\\r\\n04只有主EngineClose0返回值与动态会话官方生命周期，实际恢复流量能证明可达；二者**不能独立排除原Block未生效而过滤对象仍残留**。root已批准05补最小fresh observer，未批准独立inspect模式或任意过滤器输入。\\r\\n\\r\\n要求顺序：保留本次真实两filterId和ownedSubLayerKey→主Close0成功→新只读engine→可选只读事务→GetById两个真实ID严格返回 `FWP_E_FILTER_NOT_FOUND=0x80320003`→SubLayerGetByKey本次GUID严格返回 `FWP_E_SUBLAYER_NOT_FOUND=0x80320007`→结束只读事务并close observer。不Add对象、不改policy、不启global audit。对象仍存在、AccessDenied、泛NOT_FOUND或其他错误，均不能当精确对象已不存在。\\r\\n\\r\\nobserver中的Get/log/Abort异常也必须进入finally Close；主Close失败不启动查询来掩盖；observer失败后保留cleanup_unconfirmed，不允许后续无条件Close()覆盖成成功。闲置、从未添加对象的Close不用打开BFE；默认/--check仍须零WFP调用。独立watchdog覆盖新同步API挂起。\\r\\n\\r\\n主Agent选择的异常清理验证为：实际停止控制器心跳→lease错误→主Close及observer→ERROR_UNBLOCKED退出，随后真实同endpoint恢复正控；不需要杀helper再增加第二个人工管理员会话。这验证受控错误退出，不能表述为已测试进程崩溃/FailFast/rundown。\\r\\n\\r\\n一手依据：[FilterGetById0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmfiltergetbyid0)、[SubLayerGetByKey0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwpmu/nf-fwpmu-fwpmsublayergetbykey0)、[WFP Error Codes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/wfp-error-codes)。后两接口返回对象均须FwpmFreeMemory释放。错误码已独立查证，API权限/对象查询行为仍需真实管理员会话运行。\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. You can try changing directories.\\nL24: # FwpmFilterAdd0 function (fwpmu.h)\\nL25: \\nL26: Feedback\\nL27: \\nL28: Summarize this article for me\\nL29: \\nL30: ## In this article\\nL31: \\nL32: The FwpmFilterAdd0 function adds a new filter object to the system.\\nL33: \\nL34: ## Syntax\\nL35: \\nL36:     `DWORD FwpmFilterAdd0(\\nL37:       [in]            HANDLE               engineHandle,\\nL38:       [in]            const FWPM_FILTER0   *filter,\\nL39:       [in, optional]  PSECURITY_DESCRIPTOR sd,\\nL40:       [out, optional] UINT64               *id\\nL41:     );\\nL42:     `\\nL43: ## Parameters\\nL44: \\nL45: `[in] engineHandle`\\nL46: \\nL47: Type: HANDLE\\nL48: \\nL49: Handle for an open session to the filter engine. Call \ue200cite\ue2025†FwpmEngineOpen0\ue201 to open a session to the filter engine.\\nL50: \\nL51: `[in] filter`\\nL52: \\nL53: Type: \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPM_FILTER0\ue201 *\\nL54: \\nL55: The filter object to be added.\\nL56: \\nL57: `[in, optional] sd`\\nL58: \\nL59: Type: \ue200cite\ue2027†SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR\ue201 L60: \\nL61: Security information about the filter object.\\nL62: \\nL63: `[out, optional] id`\\nL64: \\nL65: Type: UINT64*\\nL66: \\nL67: The runtime identifier for this filter.\\nL68: ## Return value\\nL69: \\nL70: Type: DWORD\\nL71: Return code/value  | Description\\nL72: --- | ---\\nL73: ERROR_SUCCESS\\nL74: 0  | The filter was successfully added.\\nL75: ERROR_INVALID_SECURITY_DESCR\\nL76: 0x8007053A  | The security descriptor structure is invalid. Or, a filter condition contains a security descriptor in absolute format.\\nL77: FWP_E_CALLOUT_NOTIFICATION_FAILED\\nL78: 0x80320037  | The caller added a callout filter and the callout returned an error from its notification routine.\\nL79: FWP_E_* error code\\nL80: 0x80320001—0x80320039  | A Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) specific error. See \ue200cite\ue2028†WFP Error Codes\ue201 for details.\\nL81: RPC_* error code\\nL82: 0x80010001—0x80010122  | Failure to communicate with the remote or local firewall engine.\\nL83: ## Remarks\\nL84: \\nL85: FwpmFilterAdd0 adds the filter to the specified sub-layer at every filtering layer in the system.\\nL86: \\nL87: Some fields in the \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPM_FILTER0\ue201 structure are assigned by the system, not the caller, and are ignored in the call to FwpmFilterAdd0.\\nL88: \\nL89: If the caller supplies a NULL security descriptor, the system will assign a default security descriptor.\\nL90: To block connections to particular locations, add a \ue200cite\ue2029†FWP_ACTION_BLOCK\ue201 filter specifying the local address at the \ue200cite\ue20210†FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V*\ue201 layer, or add a FWP_ACTION_BLOCK filter without specifying the local address at the FWPM_LAYER_ALE_RESOURCE_ASSIGNMENT_V* layer.\\nL91: \\nL92: Note\\nL93: \\nL94: If a local address is specified at the resource assignment layer, an implicit bind would succeed because address, address type, and port may come back as \ue200cite\ue20211†FWP_EMPTY\ue201 .\\nL95: The \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPM_FILTER0\ue201 structure can label a filter as a boot-time or persistent filter. Boot-time filters are added to the Base Filtering Engine (BFE) when the TCP/IP driver starts, and are removed once the BFE finishes initialization. Persistent objects are added when the BFE starts.\\nL96: \\nL97: This function cannot be called from within a read-only transaction. It will fail with FWP_E_INCOMPATIBLE_TXN. See \ue200cite\ue20212†Object Management\ue201 for more information about transactions.\\nL98: \\nL99: The caller needs the following access rights:\\nL100:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD\ue201 access to the filter\'s container\\nL101:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\ue201 access to the provider (if any)\\nL102:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\ue201 access to the applicable layer\\nL103:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\ue201 access to the applicable sub-layer\\nL104:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\ue201 access to the callout (if any)\\nL105:   * \ue200cite\ue20213†FWPM_ACTRL_ADD_LINK\ue201 access to the provider context (if any).\\nL106: \\nL107: See \ue200cite\ue20214†Access Control\ue201 for more information.\\nL108: \\nL109: To add a filter that references a callout, invoke the functions in the following order.\\nL110:   * Call \ue200cite\ue20215†FwpsCalloutRegister0\ue201 (documented in the Windows Driver Kit (WDK)), to register the callout with the filter engine.\\nL111:   * Call \ue200cite\ue20216†FwpmCalloutAdd0\ue201 to add the callout to the system.\\nL112:   * Call FwpmFilterAdd0 to add the filter that references the callout to the system.\\nL113: \\nL114: By default filters that reference callouts that have been added but have not yet registered with the filter engine are treated as Block filters.\\nL115: FwpmFilterAdd0 is a specific implementation of FwpmFilterAdd. See \ue200cite\ue20217†WFP Version-Independent Names and Targeting Specific Versions of Windows\ue201 for more information.\\nL116: #### Examples\\nL117: The following C++ example shows how to initialize and add a filter using FwpmFilterAdd0 that\\nL118: specifically blocks traffic on IP V4 for all applications.\\nL119: \\nL120:     `\\nL121:     // Add filter to block traffic on IP V4 for all applications.\\nL122:     //\\nL123:     FWPM_FILTER0      fwpFilter;\\nL124:     FWPM_SUBLAYER0    fwpFilterSubLayer;\\nL125: \\nL126:     RtlZeroMemory(&fwpFilter, sizeof(FWPM_FILTER0));\\nL127: \\nL128:     fwpFilter.layerKey = FWPM_LAYER_ALE_AUTH_RECV_ACCEPT_V4;\\nL129:     fwpFilter.action.type = FWP_ACTION_BLOCK;\\nL130:     if (&fwpFilterSubLayer.subLayerKey != NULL)\\nL131:         fwpFilter.subLayerKey = fwpFilterSubLayer.subLayerKey;\\nL132: \\nL133:     fwpFilter.weight.type = FWP_EMPTY; // auto-weight.\\nL134:     fwpFilter.numFilterConditions = 0; // this applies to all application traffic\\nL135:     fwpFilter.displayData.name = L\\"Receive/Accept Layer Block\\";\\nL136:     fwpFilter.displayData.description = L\\"Filter to block all inbound connections.\\";\\nL137: \\nL138:     printf(\\"Adding filter to block all inbound connections.\\\\n\\");\\nL139:     result = FwpmFilterAdd0(engineHandle, &fwpFilter, NULL, NULL);\\nL140: \\nL141:     if (result != ERROR_SUCCESS)\\nL142:         printf(\\"FwpmFilterAdd0 failed. Return value: %d.\\\\n\\", result);\\nL143:     else\\nL144:         printf(\\"Filter added successfully.\\\\n\\");\\nL145: \\nL146:     `\\nL147: ## Requirements\\nL148: \\nL149: Requirement  | Value\\nL150: --- | ---\\nL151: Minimum supported client  | Windows\xa0Vista [desktop apps only]\\nL152: Minimum supported server  | Windows Server\xa02008 [desktop apps only]\\nL153: Target Platform  | Windows\\nL154: Header  | fwpmu.h\\nL155: Library  | Fwpuclnt.lib\\nL156: DLL  | Fwpuclnt.dll\\nL157: \\nL158: ## See also\\nL159: \\nL160: \ue200cite\ue2026†FWPM_FILTER0\ue201 L161: \\nL162: \ue200cite\ue20218†Management Functions\ue201 L163: \\nL164: \ue200cite\ue20219†WFP Functions\ue201 L165: \\nL166: * * *\\nL167: ## Feedback\\nL168: \\nL169: Was this page helpful?\\nL170: \\nL171: Yes No No\\nL172: \\nL173: Need help with this topic?\\nL174: \\nL175: Want to try using Ask Learn to clarify or guide you through this topic?\\nL176: \\nL177: Ask Learn Ask Learn\\nL178: \\nL179: Suggest a fix?\\nL180: \\nL181: * * *\\nL182: \\nL183: ## Additional resources\\nL184: \\nL185: * * *\\nL186: \\nL187:   * Last updated on 2021-10-13\\nL188: \\nL189: ### In this article\\nL190: \\nL191: Was this page helpful?\\nL192: \\nL193: Need help with this topic?\\nL194: \\nL195: Want to try using Ask Learn to clarify or guide you through this topic?\\nL196: \\nL197: Ask Learn Ask Learn\\nL198: \\nL199: Suggest a fix?\\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\nInternal Error ()\\n\ue200cite\ue202turn40view1\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Source: open({\\"ref_id\\":\\"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fwp/filtering-condition-identifiers\\",\\"lineno\\":null}); You can try changing directories.\\nL24: # FWPM_ACTION0 structure (fwpmtypes.h)\\nL25: \\nL26: Feedback\\nL27: \\nL28: Summarize this article for me\\nL29: \\nL30: ## In this article\\nL31: \\nL32: The FWPM_ACTION0 structure specifies the action taken if all the filter conditions are true.\\nL33: \\nL34: ## Syntax\\nL35: \\nL36:     `typedef struct FWPM_ACTION0_ {\\nL37:       FWP_ACTION_TYPE type;\\nL38:       union {\\nL39:         GUID filterType;\\nL40:         GUID calloutKey;\\nL41:       };\\nL42:     } FWPM_ACTION0;\\nL43:     `\\nL44: ## Members\\nL45: \\nL46: `type`\\nL47: \\nL48: Action type as specified by FWP_ACTION_TYPE which maps to a UINT32.\\nL49: \\nL50: Possible values:\\nL51: \\nL52: Value  | Meaning\\nL53: --- | ---\\nL54: \\nL55: FWP_ACTION_BLOCK\\nL56:  | Block the traffic. 0x00000001 | FWP_ACTION_FLAG_TERMINATING\\nL57: \\nL58: FWP_ACTION_PERMIT\\nL59:  | Permit the traffic. 0x00000002 | FWP_ACTION_FLAG_TERMINATING\\nL60: \\nL61: FWP_ACTION_CALLOUT_TERMINATING\\nL62:  | Invoke a callout that always returns block or permit. 0x00000003 | FWP_ACTION_FLAG_CALLOUT | FWP_ACTION_FLAG_TERMINATING\\nL63: FWP_ACTION_CALLOUT_INSPECTION\\nL64:  | Invoke a callout that never returns block or permit. 0x00000004 | FWP_ACTION_FLAG_CALLOUT | FWP_ACTION_FLAG_NON_TERMINATING\\nL65: \\nL66: FWP_ACTION_CALLOUT_UNKNOWN\\nL67:  | Invoke a callout that may return block or permit. 0x00000005 | FWP_ACTION_FLAG_CALLOUT\\nL68: \\nL69: `filterType`\\nL70: \\nL71: An arbitrary GUID chosen by the policy provider.\\nL72: \\nL73: Available when the action does not invoke a callout, that is, type does not contain FWP_ACTION_FLAG_CALLOUT.\\nL74: \\nL75: `calloutKey`\\nL76: \\nL77: The GUID for a valid callout in the layer.\\nL78: Available when the action invokes a callout, that is, type contains FWP_ACTION_FLAG_CALLOUT.\\nL79: ## Remarks\\nL80: \\nL81: FWPM_ACTION0 is a specific implementation of FWPM_ACTION. See \ue200cite\ue2025†WFP Version-Independent Names and Targeting Specific Versions of Windows\ue201 for more information.\\nL82: \\nL83: ## Requirements\\nL84: \\nL85: Requirement  | Value\\nL86: --- | ---\\nL87: Minimum supported client  | Windows\xa0Vista [desktop apps only]\\nL88: Minimum supported server  | Windows Server\xa02008 [desktop apps only]\\nL89: Header  | fwpmtypes.h\\nL90: \\nL91: ## See also\\nL92: \\nL93: \ue200cite\ue2026†Windows Filtering Platform API Structures\ue201 L94: \\nL95: * * *\\nL96: ## Feedback\\nL97: \\nL98: Was this page helpful?\\nL99: \\nL100: Yes No No\\nL101: \\nL102: Need help with this topic?\\nL103: \\nL104: Want to try using Ask Learn to clarify or guide you through this topic?\\nL105: \\nL106: Ask Learn Ask Learn\\nL107: \\nL108: Suggest a fix?\\nL109: \\nL110: * * *\\nL111: \\nL112: ## Additional resources\\nL113: \\nL114: * * *\\nL115: \\nL116:   * Last updated on 2024-02-22\\nL117: \\nL118: ### In this article\\nL119: \\nL120: Was this page helpful?\\nL121: \\nL122: Need help with this topic?\\nL123: \\nL124: Want to try using Ask Learn to clarify or guide you through this topic?\\nL125: \\nL126: Ask Learn Ask Learn\\nL127: \\nL128: Suggest a fix?\\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\nFWP_MATCH_TYPE (fwptypes.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fwptypes/ne-fwptypes-fwp_match_type)\\n\ue200cite\ue202turn40view3\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; Root approved a limited compatibility policy based on Microsoft\'s INDEXED lookup-acceleration semantics: Add flags remain exactly zero; pre/post-commit readback accepts exactly zero or INDEXED (0x40) alone, rejecting every other single bit and every mixture. It never logs blob content or the application path blob itself. A wrong type is recorded and rejected without interpreting its union as a blob.\\r\\n\\r\\n`scope_assertion_failed` includes stage, validationPolicy, and `failures:[{field,actual,expected}]`. The error reason is `scope_assertion_failed:<stage>:<comma-separated-fields>`. Persistent, boot-time, disabled, provider-context, action-right, unknown bits and INDEXED combined with any other bit are rejected. 系统错误码](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/debug/system-error-codes--0-499-)将5定义为访问拒绝、32为共享冲突、33为区域锁冲突。允许重读5是本次明确的有限策略；**5本身不证明共享锁，也不排除永久ACL问题**。其他winerror和缺失winerror不能仅靠errno13或异常名称纳入白名单。\n+\n+[Python OSError文档](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#OSError)区分原生winerror与近似映射errno，并提供filename/filename2；缺失值应如实记录为空，不能用推测路径冒充异常实际路径。traceback保留真实调用链，context区分read_status与heartbeat.issue，operation保留当时block/unblock/exit。\n+\n+[Python For more information, see \ue200cite\ue20213†Creating and Opening Files\ue201 , \ue200cite\ue20229†File Compression and Decompression\ue201 , and \ue200cite\ue20219†File Encryption\ue201 .\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nReplaceFileW function (winbase.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-replacefilew)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn46view3\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; Content type: text/html; Source: find({"ref_id":"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-replacefilew","pattern":"DELETE"}); Total lines: 207\nL55: This file is opened with the GENERIC_READ, DELETE, and SYNCHRONIZE access rights. The sharing mode is FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE | FILE_SHARE_DELETE.\nL56: \nL57: The caller must have write access to the file to be replaced. For more information, see \ue200cite\ue2026†File Security and Access Rights\ue201 .\nL58: \nL59: `[in] lpReplacementFileName`\nL60: \nL61: The name of the file that will replace the lpReplacedFileName file.\nL67: The function attempts to open this file with the SYNCHRONIZE, GENERIC_READ, GENERIC_WRITE, DELETE, and WRITE_DAC access rights so that it can preserve all attributes and ACLs. If this fails, the function attempts to open the file with the SYNCHRONIZE, GENERIC_READ, DELETE, and WRITE_DAC access rights. No sharing mode is specified.\nL68: \nL69: `[in, optional] lpBackupFileName`\nL123: The ReplaceFile function combines several steps within a single function. An application can call ReplaceFile instead of calling separate functions to save the data to a new file, rename the original file using a temporary name, rename the new file to have the same name as the original file, and delete the original file. Another advantage is that ReplaceFile not only copies the new file data, but also preserves the following attributes of the original file:\nL124:   * Creation time\nL125:   * Short file name\nL126:   * Object identifier\nL127:   * DACLs\nL128:   * Security resource attributes\nL129:   * Encryption\nL130:   * Compression\nL131:   * Named streams not already in the replacement file\nL132: For example, if the replacement file is encrypted, but the replaced file is not encrypted, the resulting file is not encrypted.\nL133: Windows\xa07, Windows Server\xa02008\xa0R2, Windows Server\xa02008, Windows\xa0Vista, Windows Server\xa02003 and Windows\xa0XP:\xa0\xa0Security resource attributes (ATTRIBUTE_SECURITY_INFORMATION) for the original file are not preserved until Windows\xa08 and Windows Server\xa02012.\nL134: \nL135: Note\nL136: \nL137: If the replacement file is protected using \ue200cite\ue2029†Selective Wipe\ue201 , then the replaced file will be protected by the enterprise id of the replacement file.\nL138: \nL139: \nL140: \nL141: The resulting file has the same file ID as the replacement file.\nL142: The backup file, replaced file, and replacement file must all reside on the same volume.\nL143: To delete or rename a file, you must have either delete permission on the file or delete child permission in the parent directory. If you set up a directory with all access except delete and delete child and the DACLs of new files are inherited, then you should be able to create a file without being able to delete it. However, you can then create a file, and you will get all the access you request on the handle returned to you at the time you create the file.\nL144: If you requested delete permission at the time you created the file, you could delete or rename the file with that handle but not with any other.\nL145: Note\nL146: \nL147: The winbase.h header defines ReplaceFile as an alias that automatically selects the ANSI or Unicode version of this function based on the definition of the UNICODE preprocessor constant.
